papers.title: Creation of the Universe in Lorentzian Classical Gravity
papers.authors: Avipsa Chakrabarti, Avik Chakraborty, Mart\'in Molina, Ayan Mukhopadhyay, Salom\'{o}n Romero
papers.abstract: The singularity theorems and the past incompleteness of inflationary spacetimes suggest that the beginning of the Universe lies beyond the domain of semiclassical gravity. We show that the creation of the Universe can nevertheless be understood within Lorentzian gravity by allowing gravitational junctions, so that the full spacetime need not be a smooth manifold. We construct rotationally invariant cosmic creation gates joining any finite number $n\geq2$ of locally de Sitter regions in $D\geq3$ spacetime dimensions at a timelike perfect-fluid junction with $P=w\rho$. For $w>-(D-3)/(D-2)$, they are geodesically complete in both temporal directions. The total spatial volume approaches finite, positive limits in the infinite past and future on the global-time foliation adapted to the junction fluid. We also construct exact deformed cosmic creation gates through nonlinear homogeneous backreaction that retain the initial volume while the future volume grows without bound. In these solutions, the junction fluid always expands, cooling for $w>0$ and heating for allowed $w<0$. Keeping the bulk regions locally de Sitter, we determine the linearized perturbations: in three dimensions, the generic inhomogeneous sector contains one hybrid sound mode and $n-1$ relative transverse modes; in four and higher dimensions, only the homogeneous hybrid sound mode survives. A finite-volume beginning requires fine-tuned homogeneous and inhomogeneous initial data, while causal response generically leads to unbounded future spatial volume. We also discuss a broader creation criterion allowing bounded past-volume oscillations. The gravitational equations determine conditioned admissible histories. We discuss implications for cosmology.
papers.summary: This paper constructs Lorentzian junctions that allow a geodesically complete, finite-volume birth of the Universe from multiple de Sitter patches, and analyzes their linearized perturbations, showing that only a hybrid sound mode survives in higher dimensions. It offers a classical gravity framework for cosmological creation that could inform de Sitter holography and early-Universe dynamics.

papers.title: Black Hole Entropy from Entangled Quantum Reference Frames
papers.abstract: In the extended phase space of Donnelly and Freidel, the edge modes of a Schwarzschild black hole are dynamical reference frames whose phase space is the cotangent bundle of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$. Gluing the two exterior regions at the bifurcation point leaves a single canonical pair. Within the extended phase space, this pair can be described either by Kucha\v{r}'s mass and difference of asymptotic times or by the area and the relative rapidity of the two frames, which are two gauge choices of the same system. The latter is the pair of Carlip and Teitelboim, and the relative rapidity is the time shift of the crossed product construction. We quantize the frames in this gauge and construct the gravitational entangling product of the two exteriors. Requiring the frames to be causal restricts them to the semigroup $\mathrm{SL}^+(2,\mathbb{R})$, whose Plancherel measure yields the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy as the entanglement entropy between the two exteriors, together with a logarithmic correction, both independent of the ultraviolet cutoff.
papers.summary: The paper shows that the edge modes of a Schwarzschild black hole form a dynamical reference frame described by SL(2,R) and that gluing the two exteriors yields a single canonical pair. Quantizing these frames in a causal gauge leads to an entanglement entropy that reproduces the Bekenstein–Hawking area law with a logarithmic correction, independent of UV cutoffs.

papers.title: Holomorphic fermions in $\text{AdS}_{2}$
papers.authors: Calvin Y. -R. Chen, Lukas W. Lindwasser
papers.abstract: On two-dimensional Anti-de Sitter space, Majorana fermions with a discrete set of finely tuned, non-zero mass parameters possess conserved spinor--tensors that are symmetric and traceless. In complex coordinates, these correspond to pairs of holomorphic and anti-holomorphic half-integer spin currents and admit Laurent series mode expansions reminiscent of standard two-dimensional conformal field theories. We exploit this fact in order to fully parameterise the classical phase space associated with the equation of motion in terms of arbitrary (anti-)holomorphic functions. We further show that this parameterisation can be written covariantly in terms of a conformal Killing spinor--tensor, hinting at a hidden conformal symmetry. We also show they possess chiral algebras which are strict subalgebras of the one present in the corresponding theory on flat space.
papers.summary: This work shows that Majorana fermions on AdS₂ with finely tuned masses admit conserved symmetric traceless spinor‑tensors that, in complex coordinates, become holomorphic and anti‑holomorphic half‑integer spin currents. The authors use this structure to parametrize the classical phase space via arbitrary holomorphic functions and uncover a hidden conformal symmetry, suggesting a chiral algebra that is a strict subalgebra of the flat‑space counterpart.

papers.title: Quiver Lab -- A Computing Tool for Quiver Gauge Theories
papers.abstract: Quiver Lab is a browser-based workspace for drawing quivers and exploring the moduli spaces of three-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = 4$ theories. It computes Higgs and Coulomb branch Hilbert series, plethystic logarithms, supported refinements, and Decay and Fission Hasse diagrams. This note explains the Light and Expert workflows and the main computational methods
papers.summary: Quiver Lab is a web-based tool that lets users draw quiver gauge theories and compute their Higgs and Coulomb branch Hilbert series, plethystic logarithms, and Hasse diagrams, providing a practical workflow for exploring 3D $mathcal{N}=4$ moduli spaces. It offers both light and expert modes, making advanced computational techniques accessible to researchers working on quiver dynamics and related moduli space problems.

papers.title: Go with the flow(s): radial de Sitter holography and $T^2 (+ \Lambda_2)$
papers.abstract: What can we learn about a putative dual to de Sitter spacetime from the bulk? Conversely, what can a candidate dual theory teach us about the bulk? In this work, we construct midisuperspace Wheeler-DeWitt states that are localised on the Schwarzschild-de Sitter spacetime. Using these states, we construct a slice-independent worldtube holographic framework in the static patch. We then construct a dictionary between this worldtube proposal and both the $T^2$ and $T^2 + \Lambda_2$ frameworks for cut-off holography. In doing so, we provide a bulk realisation of $T^2+ \Lambda_2$ for dS$_4$ black holes. We identify the average Hamiltonian of our worldtube proposal as the seed energy of the $T^2 (+ \Lambda_2)$ theories. To recover the $T^2 (+ \Lambda_2)$ energy spectrum as the average Hamiltonian of a worldtube theory, one must make the bulk framework slice-dependent, and we discuss the consequences of this trade-off.
papers.summary: This paper develops a slice‑independent worldtube holographic description of Schwarzschild‑de Sitter spacetimes and matches it to cut‑off holography frameworks based on T^2 and T^2+Λ_2 deformations. It shows how the average Hamiltonian of the worldtube theory reproduces the energy spectrum of these deformed theories, highlighting a trade‑off between slice independence and spectral recovery.

papers.title: Differential Equations for Dressed "in-in" Correlators
papers.abstract: We extend the formalism of differential equations and Integration-by-Parts identities, to cosmological in-in correlators of conformally coupled scalar fields, that can be formulated as dressed flat space amplitudes. These differential equations turn out to be quite powerful for extracting information about the class of functions which the corresponding amplitudes integrate to. Furthermore, they can be formulated algorithmically. Here we illustrate this for the cosmological bubble- triangle and exchange diagram.
papers.summary: This work extends differential-equation and IBP techniques to cosmological in‑in correlators of conformally coupled scalars, recasting them as dressed flat‑space amplitudes. The authors demonstrate the method on bubble‑triangle and exchange diagrams, showing how the equations constrain the analytic structure of the resulting correlators.

papers.title: Near-horizon BF bounds for the $t^+$ KK tower on extremal AdS$_5$ black holes
papers.authors: Xiao-Long Liu, Zheng Miao, Yuezhang Tang
papers.abstract: We study the charged Breitenlohner--Freedman (BF) bound for all horizon harmonics of the type IIB $t^+$ Kaluza--Klein tower on extremal charged AdS$_5$ black holes with equal rotations. The scalar equation follows from maximal five-dimensional gauged supergravity at level zero and the linearized exceptional-field-theory equations at higher levels. For aligned charge and rotation, a quadratic form in charge and spin changes signature on the curve of supersymmetric (BPS) black holes, where every mode satisfies the bound. Above the curve, where $\Omega_H>1$, every black hole has a violating mode, although no finite truncation in level or spin detects violation at every such black hole. Below the curve, where $\Phi_H>1$, the BF-passing set is confined to a thin strip and controlled by charge and spin discreteness. At large radius and fixed rotation, a level-four mode with spin proportional to the radius violates the bound even where all U(2) singlets satisfy it. These results concern the near-horizon BF bound of one tower in two-derivative supergravity; full radial stability remains open.
papers.summary: The paper analyzes the Breitenlohner–Freedman stability bound for the full Kaluza–Klein tower of type IIB supergravity modes on extremal rotating AdS$_5$ black holes, revealing a sharp transition at the supersymmetric curve where all modes satisfy the bound and a regime above it where every black hole hosts a violating mode. It also shows that even when all U(2) singlets are stable, higher-spin, higher-level modes can violate the bound, leaving the full radial stability of these solutions unresolved.

papers.title: Quotient Quiver Subtraction -- Product Groups
papers.authors: Sam Bennett, Amihay Hanany, Guhesh Kumaran
papers.abstract: Quotient quiver subtraction translates the gauging of Coulomb branch global symmetries into a combinatoric operation on 3d $\mathcal{N}=4$ gauge theories. This work uses brane systems to introduce a systematic method to gauge $\textrm{U}(n)\times\textrm{U}(n')$ and $\textrm{SU}(n)\times\textrm{SU}(n')$ emergent Coulomb branch global symmetries. Similar to other recently-introduced techniques, the gauging operation is a two-step process; in this case, it involves the symplectisation of unitary gauge factors into symplectic groups. A host of explicit examples are used to verify the procedure, and connections are made to Class $\mathcal{S}$ theories and three-dimensional theories realising maximal implosion spaces.
papers.summary: This paper develops a combinatorial procedure called quotient quiver subtraction to implement gauging of emergent Coulomb branch global symmetries in 3d N=4 gauge theories, using brane constructions to systematically promote unitary gauge factors to symplectic groups. The authors illustrate the method with explicit examples and connect the resulting theories to Class S constructions and maximal implosion spaces, offering new tools for studying symmetry gauging in low-dimensional gauge dynamics.

papers.title: Covering Surfaces, Conical-Defect Continuation, and Multi-Entropy at Arbitrary Genus
papers.abstract: We derive normalized geometric factors for permutation-twist correlators at arbitrary genus. For three uniformly ramified branch values, hypergeometric uniformization shows that the real part of the continued conical-defect exponent equals the covering-space anomaly factor. Its imaginary part is an Euler-characteristic Weyl phase. We extend the normalization to additional branch values, derive higher replica-index corrections to the geometric multi-entropy, and state the extra condition required for a holographic limit. A reducible conformal/topological example demonstrates why large central charge alone does not fix the complete entanglement result.
papers.summary: This paper derives normalized geometric factors for permutation-twist correlators on arbitrary-genus covering surfaces, linking the real part of conical-defect exponents to covering-space anomaly factors and the imaginary part to an Euler-characteristic Weyl phase. It extends these results to higher replica indices, identifies conditions for a holographic limit, and shows that large central charge alone does not determine the full entanglement structure.

papers.title: Entropically favored scalar hair on AdS black branes
papers.abstract: We construct neutral AdS$_5$ black branes with source-free scalar hair that is entropically favored over the symmetric phase. A quadratic scalar--Gauss--Bonnet coupling destabilizes the thermal state while leaving the ultraviolet operator dimension fixed at $\Delta=3$. The fully backreacted solutions require only a quadratic scalar potential. We describe how a neural-network search led to this simple model.
papers.summary: The authors construct neutral AdS5 black branes with scalar hair that is entropically favored over the symmetric phase, using a quadratic scalar–Gauss–Bonnet coupling that destabilizes the thermal state while keeping the UV operator dimension fixed at Δ=3. The fully backreacted solutions are obtained with only a quadratic scalar potential, and a neural‑network search guided the discovery of this simple model.

papers.title: Circuit complexity of coupled four-mode squeezed states in two-field inflation
papers.authors: Tao Li, Hai-Bing Fu, Lei-Hua Liu
papers.abstract: We study the circuit complexity of coupled curvature and entropy perturbations in two-field inflation. We start from the quadratic action and derive the full Hamiltonian. The Hamiltonian includes all diagonal and off-diagonal quadratic terms. We then obtain three coupled equations for the pair amplitudes of the four-mode squeezed state. From these amplitudes, we calculate the two principal squeezing strengths. We use them to determine the Nielsen circuit complexity. For an equal-weight Gaussian circuit, the complexity takes the form $\mathcal{C}_{2,k}=\sqrt{2(r_{1k}^{2}+r_{2k}^{2})}$. It depends on the squeezing strengths but not explicitly on the squeezing angles. Our numerical results show that the complexity grows after horizon crossing in both coupled and uncoupled models. Interfield coupling changes the pair amplitudes and the four-mode squeezed state. However, its effect on the circuit complexity is small for the parameters considered. This result shows that different four-mode pair-amplitude matrices can yield similar values of the chosen equal-weight circuit complexity. The present calculation provides a reference for studying Gaussian circuit complexity in more general two-field inflationary models.
papers.summary: This paper analyzes the Nielsen circuit complexity of coupled curvature and entropy perturbations in two-field inflation by deriving the full quadratic Hamiltonian and solving for the four-mode squeezed state amplitudes. The authors find that interfield coupling has only a modest effect on complexity, which grows after horizon crossing, offering a benchmark for Gaussian complexity in multi-field inflationary scenarios.

papers.title: Tachyon and massless sectors of the bosonic string effective action
papers.abstract: Recently, it has been observed that in certain schemes of the bosonic string effective action, the non-derivative tachyon appears only in the tachyon potential, while all other couplings involve covariant derivatives of the tachyon and massless fields. Within these schemes, a minimal basis can be found whose coupling constants are constrained by T-duality upon circle reduction. Using this constraint, one obtains sets of couplings at each order of \(\alpha'\) that are invariant under Buscher rules supplemented by higher-derivative corrections for all base-space fields except the tachyon. In this paper, we observe that consistency of these T-dual sets with S-matrix elements requires an appropriate field redefinition, such that each set becomes invariant under Buscher rules supplemented by higher-derivative corrections for all base-space fields except the metric, dilaton, and tachyon. This separates the couplings into a massless sector and a tachyon sector. We determine the six-derivative couplings in the massless sector, with all coupling constants fixed, and find two T-dual couplings in the tachyon sector with arbitrary coupling constants. We show that the leading-order action and the massless-sector couplings exactly reproduce the expansion of the sphere-level S-matrix element of two tachyons and two massless vertex operators at six-momentum order, and that the coupling constant of the four-tachyon coupling in the tachyon sector is fixed by the expansion of the four-tachyon S-matrix element at six-momentum order.
papers.summary: The paper constructs a minimal basis of higher-derivative couplings in the bosonic string effective action that respect T-duality, separating massless and tachyon sectors, and fixes all six-derivative massless couplings by matching to sphere-level S-matrix elements. It also identifies two undetermined tachyon couplings and determines the four-tachyon coupling constant from the six-momentum expansion of the four-tachyon amplitude.

papers.title: The Topological String on the Quintic to Genus 83 and the Rank-Two D4-D2-D0 Indices
papers.abstract: We compute quintic Gopakumar-Vafa invariants for genera 2-83 and degrees up to 44 by integrating the holomorphic anomaly equations. Under rank-one modularity for the required Gieseker invariants and rank-two charge conjugation, a coupled system of boundary and surplus wall-crossing equations fixes the holomorphic ambiguities and 22 of the 36 polar rank-two D4-D2-D0 coefficients, without assuming any rank-two index. A computer-assisted extension of wall crossing supplies additional equations and the boundary datum needed to close the recursion through genus 83. With known low-genus input, the GV data are complete through degree 32 and yield PT and DT tables. Selected higher-genus wall-crossing invariants reach genus 216; 33 entries require additional hypotheses. Retrospectively selected extrapolations give conditional candidates at genera 84 and 85 and, with rank-two mock modularity, for the remaining polar coefficients.
papers.summary: This paper computes Gopakumar-Vafa invariants for the quintic Calabi-Yau up to genus 83 using holomorphic anomaly equations and wall-crossing, determining many rank‑two D4‑D2‑D0 BPS indices. It provides extensive tables of GV, PT, and DT invariants and explores modularity constraints for higher‑genus contributions.

papers.title: Resurgence and Modularity in the First Painlev\'e Equation
papers.abstract: For the first Painlev\'e equation, we relate three nonlinear Stokes maps associated with a full turn around infinity to modular transformations of the two-parameter tau function through the identity $\boldsymbol S_\pi\circ\boldsymbol S_0\circ \boldsymbol S_{-\pi}=\mathsf S\circ\mathsf T$. Here the subscripts label Borel directions, while $\mathsf S$ and $\mathsf T$ denote the modular generators. Working under the analytic assumptions of the topological recursion and exact WKB constructions, we compare Stokes multipliers of the associated isomonodromy system while tracking the homology basis of its elliptic spectral curve under rotations of the independent variable. For the sectors considered, we identify the known parameter transformation induced by an $8\pi/5$ rotation with the modular $T$-action and derive a new explicit parameter relation realizing the $S$-action for a $2\pi/5$ rotation. We also determine the multiplicative factors in the corresponding tau-function relations, including their normalization constants. Together, these results give an explicit realization of single-valuedness after one full turn around infinity for both the Painlev\'e transcendent and its tau function, with the tau-function prefactors cancelling by Abel's five-term identity for the Rogers dilogarithm.
papers.summary: This work connects the nonlinear Stokes phenomena of the first Painlevé equation to modular transformations of its tau function, showing how a full rotation around infinity corresponds to the modular S and T generators. By tracking the elliptic spectral curve’s homology under variable rotations, the authors derive explicit parameter relations and demonstrate single‑valuedness via the Rogers dilogarithm identity.

papers.title: The Non-Relativistic Limit of Five-Dimensional Boson Stars and Scale Invariance Violation
papers.authors: Eduard Kim, Oleg Kondrashov, Emin Nugaev, Yakov Shnir
papers.abstract: We investigate the non-relativistic limit of spherically symmetric boson stars in (4+1)-dimensional general relativity (GR). In this limit, the resulting Newtonian theory exhibits an exact scale invariance, leading to a critical boson star configuration with a fixed global U(1) charge and vanishing binding energy. We identify the origin of these properties in the restored scale symmetry and analyze how relativistic and gravitational corrections break this symmetry. By comparing the full (4+1)-dimensional Einstein-Klein-Gordon system with the Wick-Cutkosky model, we quantify the effects of these corrections on the energy-charge relation and the kinematic stability of the configurations. Our results demonstrate how weak violation of scale invariance lifts the degeneracy of the non-relativistic solutions and determines the behavior of boson stars away from the critical limit.
papers.summary: The paper studies the non‑relativistic limit of spherically symmetric boson stars in five‑dimensional general relativity, revealing an exact scale invariance that fixes the global U(1) charge and yields zero binding energy. It then quantifies how relativistic and gravitational corrections break this symmetry, lifting the degeneracy and determining the stability of near‑critical configurations.

papers.title: Conformal Spectrum of (Super) Chiral Ising and XY Models
papers.authors: Oleg Antipin, Jahmall Bersini, Jacob Hafjall, Giulia Muco, Francesco Sannino
papers.abstract: We determine the spectrum of scaling dimensions of composite operators in the critical Gross-Neveu-Yukawa and Nambu-Jona-Lasinio-Yukawa models through a next-to-leading order semiclassical computation. Their infrared fixed points belong to the chiral Ising and chiral XY universality classes, respectively. At next-to-leading order, we resolve the Lorentz structure of the operator spectrum. For the parameter values at which supersymmetry is expected to emerge in the infrared, we obtain a closed-form expression encoding the full spectrum within the semiclassical methodology. The resulting organization of operators into superconformal multiplets provides further evidence for emergent superconformal dynamics.
papers.summary: The paper computes the scaling dimensions of composite operators in the Gross–Neveu–Yukawa and Nambu–Jona–Lasinio–Yukawa models, identifying the infrared fixed points with the chiral Ising and chiral XY universality classes. At the supersymmetric point it gives a closed-form spectrum that organizes operators into superconformal multiplets, supporting emergent superconformal dynamics.

papers.title: Bootstrapping Wilson lines in Critical Bosonic QED$_3$ Part 1: Large-$N$ endpoint correlators and CFT data
papers.authors: Jun Maeda, Toshiki Onagi, Soichiro Shimamori
papers.abstract: We study the conformal Wilson line with general charge $q$ in critical bosonic QED$_3$ with $N$ complex scalar flavors by combining diagrammatic four-point calculations with endpoint crossing. We formulate the endpoint crossing equations with the full $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ flavor structure, keeping positivity manifest. For arbitrary positive integer charge $q$ held fixed at large $N$, we obtain closed-form expressions for four-endpoint correlators and mixed correlators involving two bulk Hubbard--Stratonovich fields through first subleading order in $1/N$. These results determine the endpoint dimension, the defect $g$-function, and the dimensions and endpoint OPE coefficients of the lowest non-singlet Wilson-line primaries. Moreover, combining the diagrammatic correlator with endpoint crossing, somewhat surprisingly, we find agreement between the bulk and Wilson-line spectra in every non-singlet flavor channel through order $1/N$. At degenerate levels, this agreement concerns the OPE-weighted averages of anomalous dimensions probed by the endpoint correlator. For unit charge, we independently reproduce these averages from the known bulk higher-spin spectrum.
papers.summary: The authors compute the large‑N expansion of Wilson‑line endpoint correlators in critical bosonic QED3, solving the full SU(N) crossing equations and extracting endpoint dimensions, g‑functions, and non‑singlet operator data to O(1/N). They find remarkable agreement between bulk higher‑spin spectra and defect data, including OPE‑weighted anomalous dimensions, and reproduce known results for unit charge.

papers.title: Topological interfaces between universes and generalized families of 2d QFTs
papers.authors: Pinak Banerjee, Yuhan Gai, Alonso Perez-Lona, Daniel Robbins, Subham Roy, Eric Sharpe, with an appendix by Xingyang Yu
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional quantum field theories with topological point operators decompose into universes. Just as fusion categories have played an important role in understanding non-invertible symmetries, multi-fusion categories play an analogous role for the symmetries of such decomposing theories. We describe a finite symmetry as a multi-fusion category together with its action functor, which keeps track of trivially acting symmetries and of the topological interfaces between universes. Relative to a chosen symmetry, we classify pairs of universes by the topological interfaces it contains, which reflect the structure of the multi-fusion category: universes in different indecomposable summands are joined by no interface (Type~III), while within a summand they are related by invertible (Type~I) or only non-invertible (Type~II) interfaces. For orbifolds with a trivially acting abelian normal subgroup, we derive the full inherited symmetry, which characterizes the operators between universes found case by case by Robbins, Sharpe and Vandermeulen and yields pairs of Types~I and~II but never of Type~III. We construct Type~III pairs instead from extensions of $2$-group type and from renormalization group flows out of a common ultraviolet theory. Finally, we propose a correspondence with the generalized families of quantum field theories of Brennan and Intriligator, in which equivariant families correspond to Type~I pairs and categorical ones to Type~II pairs whose gauging preserves the symmetry, family anomalies appear as universes carrying different symmetry-protected topological phases, and Type~III pairs can realize families over a discrete parameter. An appendix by Xingyang Yu works out the higher-charge Schwinger model as a Lagrangian example.
papers.summary: This paper studies how 2d QFTs with topological point operators split into distinct universes and how multi-fusion categories encode the symmetries and interfaces between them. It classifies universes by the types of interfaces (invertible, non-invertible, or absent) and connects these structures to orbifold symmetries, 2-group extensions, RG flows, and generalized families of QFTs.

papers.title: The Effective Field Theory Origin of the Fuzzy Sphere Method
papers.abstract: Fuzzy sphere Hamiltonians for (2+1)D conformal field theories are usually written directly on the lowest Landau level. We introduce a framework organizing them as descendants of local ``mother theories'' on $S^2\times\mathbb R$. We start with the example of Ising mother theory built from two charged Dirac fermions coupled to a real mediator $\phi$. Integrating out $\phi$ and the higher Landau levels produces the fuzzy Hamiltonian, while integrating out the fermions gives a conventional local $\phi$ effective field theory flowing to the Ising point. Mild modifications of the same theory reach the Gaussian point (tricritical route) and the Lee-Yang continuation. Exploring the space of mother theories, we next promote $\phi$ to a complex field $\Phi$ and construct a new example, whose descendant is an easy-plane ferromagnet on the fuzzy sphere. Its spontaneous symmetry breaking phase gives a pseudo-Goldstone relativistic scalar, similar to the model introduced by Y.-C. He, while its critical point is non-relativistic, providing the first example of $z=2$ scaling on the fuzzy sphere. Remarkably, it admits exact one-magnon solutions, and the $z=2$ critical point can be found analytically. We then outline a rich landscape of further applications of our approach.
papers.summary: This paper develops a framework for constructing fuzzy sphere Hamiltonians as descendants of local mother theories on S^2×R, exemplified by an Ising model built from charged Dirac fermions coupled to a mediator field. It further extends the construction to a complex mediator yielding an easy‑plane ferromagnet on the fuzzy sphere, featuring a relativistic pseudo‑Goldstone mode and an analytically solvable z=2 critical point.

papers.title: Unifying energy-entropy bounds in semiclassical gravity
papers.abstract: We revisit bounds on energy and entropy in semiclassical gravity, aiming to strengthen and unify established bounds, in particular the quantum focussing conjecture (QFC) and the smeared null energy condition (SNEC). Both the QFC and SNEC have important applications and are the strongest in their respective hierarchies; however, neither implies the other, nor reduces to the null energy condition (NEC) in the classical limit. To that end, we define a new class of bounds dubbed gravitational energy-entropy conditions (GEECs) that imply both the QFC and SNEC, and reduce to the NEC classically. We construct an explicit family of GEECs by imposing the defining criteria on a broad set of stress tensor bounds, and constrain its remaining parameter space through test cases, in an effective field theory-inspired approach. Our GEECs are powerful candidate bounds on energy and entropy in semiclassical gravity.
papers.summary: The authors introduce gravitational energy‑entropy conditions (GEECs) that simultaneously imply the quantum focussing conjecture and the smeared null energy condition while reducing to the classical null energy condition. They construct a family of such bounds via stress‑tensor inequalities and test them in an effective field theory framework, offering a unified constraint on energy and entropy in semiclassical gravity.

papers.title: Collective Bootstrap for Matrix Quantum Mechanics
papers.abstract: We develop a collective bootstrap framework for large $N$ matrix quantum mechanics formulated directly in the loop space of single trace coordinate moments. Loop joining and splitting operations organize the kinetic constraints systematically and avoid treating momentum containing moments as independent variables. Employing the virial theorem, a Schur complement, and a relaxation of quadratic products of loops, we recast the nonlinear constrained optimization of the collective energy into a semidefinite program, which yields a lower bound on the planar ground state energy at every truncation. A sequential semidefinite optimization heuristic then searches for configurations satisfying planar factorization and estimates the ground state energy and loop expectation values. Applications to one-, two-, and three-matrix models exhibit close agreement with analytic solutions and master field optimization. By working exclusively with coordinate moments, the framework permits truncations at higher word length and offers a promising approach to models with more matrices, including the bosonic sectors of the BFSS and BMN models.
papers.summary: This work introduces a collective bootstrap approach for large‑N matrix quantum mechanics, formulating the problem in loop space and converting the constrained optimization into a semidefinite program that yields rigorous lower bounds on planar ground‑state energies. The method is validated on one‑, two‑ and three‑matrix models and offers a scalable framework for more complex systems such as the bosonic sectors of BFSS and BMN, potentially informing holographic studies.

papers.title: Elliptic master integrals and the one-loop cosmological wavefunction
papers.abstract: Loop corrections to the cosmological wavefunction involve similar integrals to those required for scattering amplitudes. For the one-loop triangle of a conformally coupled scalar, the master integrals are elliptic, and so the triangle wavefunction coefficient was expected to be elliptic as well. Using a bootstrap approach, we compute this triangle coefficient exactly and show that it is not: the elliptic periods cancel, and the flat-space wavefunction coefficient is a combination of dilogarithms. The cancellation occurs because the residue of the loop integrand on the elliptic sector is a flat-space amplitude, rational in the loop momentum. The one-loop box, by contrast, is not polylogarithmic, even with a single external leg at each site. Its threshold discontinuity involves elliptic integrals, which we also give in closed form. For regular-tetrahedron momenta the periods of a K3 surface enter its loop integrand.
papers.summary: The authors compute the one‑loop triangle contribution to the cosmological wavefunction for a conformally coupled scalar and find that the expected elliptic structure cancels, leaving a dilogarithmic expression. They also analyze the one‑loop box, showing it remains non‑polylogarithmic with elliptic threshold discontinuities and K3 surface periods for symmetric momenta.

papers.title: From pq-webs to magnetic quivers and back I: dictionary and deformations
papers.authors: Sebastiano Garavaglia, Sara Pasquetti, Palash Singh
papers.abstract: This is the first of two companion papers in which we study five-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ theories engineered by $(p,q)$ five-brane webs and their associated three-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=4$ magnetic quivers. We focus on the $N+\mathrm{SU}(N)_0^{k-1}+N$ box quiver theories. We propose an exact parameter dictionary relating the five-dimensional flavour masses and instanton couplings to the Fayet-Iliopoulos parameters of the corresponding strong-coupling magnetic quiver.   We test this dictionary through a broad class of deformations, including mass deformations, weak-coupling limits, and vacuum expectation values. On the five-dimensional side, we implement these flows directly at the level of the superconformal index. The dictionary fixes the corresponding FI deformations and monopole VEVs. We analyse them in the magnetic-quiver squashed-sphere partition function using a new method that tracks Higgsing, decoupled sectors, and infrared theories. Our results promote magnetic quivers to tools for the quantitative study of how the five-dimensional superconformal index responds to deformations. Once the parameter dictionary is known, exact three-dimensional observables can be used to reconstruct the corresponding five-dimensional physics and to navigate the full deformation network in both directions.
papers.summary: This paper establishes a precise dictionary between parameters of five‑dimensional (mathcal{N}=1) theories engineered from ((p,q)) five‑brane webs and the Fayet‑Iliopoulos parameters of their three‑dimensional (mathcal{N}=4) magnetic quivers, and tests it via deformations and index computations.

papers.title: From pq-webs to magnetic quivers and back II: distributional indices and 5d theories breaking bad
papers.authors: Sebastiano Garavaglia, Sara Pasquetti, Palash Singh
papers.abstract: This is the second of two companion papers in which we study five-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ theories engineered by $(p,q)$ five-brane webs and their associated three-dimensional magnetic quivers. Leveraging the exact parameter dictionary between the $N+\mathrm{SU}(N)_0^{k-1}+N$ theories and their magnetic quivers at infinite coupling, proposed in the first paper, we investigate nilpotent moment-map VEV deformations and their three-dimensional counterparts. We show that, when the Higgsing is excessive, the five-dimensional superconformal index becomes distributional, mirroring a characteristic feature of bad and broken theories in three dimensions. We also develop a five-brane web interpretation of these results, identifying the Hanany-Witten moves associated with the Higgsing cascade and relating inequivalent frames to distinct tessellations of the generalised toric diagram.
papers.summary: This paper extends the study of 5d N=1 SCFTs engineered by (p,q) five‑brane webs, showing that excessive Higgsing produces distributional superconformal indices, a hallmark of bad/broken 3d theories. It maps the Higgsing cascade to Hanany‑Witten moves and relates distinct brane frames to different tessellations of the generalized toric diagram, providing a five‑brane web interpretation of magnetic quiver deformations.

papers.title: Holography and localization in fractional field theory
papers.abstract: Fractional field theory is a promising framework wherein to quantize the gravitational interaction but the presence of nonlocal operators can make its handling difficult. With the purpose of easing this problem, we recast the theory as a local dual in two ways. First, we generalize the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension theorem to self-adjoint fractional field theories with multi-scale kinetic terms and nonlocal interactions, taking the example of a scalar field. The latter is reinterpreted as a nonlocal boundary degree of freedom holographically dual to a local theory of two scalars living in a higher-dimensional bulk. However, inclusion of a local non-linear potential is not straightforward. We therefore propose an alternative picture where the nonlocal theory is not extended to a higher-dimensional space but is localized at the price of introducing a continuum of masses. This \emph{spectral localization} allows for a natural implementation of the fakeon prescription and the related classicization procedure, already employed in local theories with higher-derivative and complex ghosts. Applications to fractional quantum gravity and its comparison with quadratic quantum gravity are discussed.
papers.summary: The paper extends the Caffarelli–Silvestre theorem to self‑adjoint fractional field theories, recasting nonlocal scalar dynamics as a local dual with two bulk scalars and also via a spectral localization that introduces a continuum of masses. This framework enables the application of the fakeon prescription and classicization in fractional quantum gravity, offering a comparison with quadratic gravity.

papers.title: Gravitational Reconstruction in $AdS_{4}$
papers.authors: David A. Lowe, Yiru Wang, Juanyi Yang
papers.abstract: We reconstruct linearized gravitational perturbations in $AdS_{4}$ from a conserved, traceless stress tensor on a fixed conformally flat boundary metric, extending our earlier real Lorentzian construction. For admissible data with no spacelike Fourier support in a flat conformal frame, the physical response reduces to an integral over boundary light-cone cuts. Boundary improvements restore Fefferman--Graham (FG) gauge while preserving normalizability and the linearized Weyl tensor. We then reconstruct perturbations with general spacelike boundary momentum, including nonzero frequency and its zero-frequency limit, using explicit position-space generalized functions on real stress data. Boundary kernels are constructed for normalizable perturbations and sufficient conditions are derived for the reconstruction to converge. The results motivate controlled flat-space limits relevant to Bondi--Metzner--Sachs symmetries and celestial holography.
papers.summary: This work reconstructs linearized gravitational perturbations in AdS4 from a conserved, traceless boundary stress tensor, extending a Lorentzian construction to include general spacelike boundary momentum and zero-frequency limits. The authors provide explicit position-space kernels, establish convergence criteria, and discuss implications for flat-space limits, BMS symmetries, and celestial holography.

papers.title: Generalized Symmetries of QED$_4$ on Non-Spin Manifolds
papers.abstract: Generalized symmetries are sensitive to the tangential structure of spacetime. We study this interplay for massless QED on oriented non-spin four-manifolds, where the photon becomes a spin$^c$ connection and the path integral sums over spin$^c$ structures. The shifted flux quantization extends the magnetic 1-form symmetry into a $w_2$-twisted 1-form symmetry: its $2\pi$ rotation acts as a gravitational sign, fixed by the normal bundle of the surface the operator wraps. The obstruction to treating it as an ordinary magnetic 1-form symmetry is an order-two mixed magnetic-gravitational anomaly, which is classified by reduced oriented bordism and detected on the Wu manifold. In a fixed spin$^c$ sector, this anomaly is removable by a counterterm, so it is a property of the sum over spin$^c$ structures. We discuss its consequences for gapped, Coulomb, and Higgs phases. The chiral anomaly is governed by the index of the spin$^c$ Dirac operator, so rational chiral defects carry gravitational as well as electromagnetic responses. A spin$^c$ Hall topological field theory cancels the electromagnetic part but leaves a framing anomaly. At the level of anomaly inflow, this is canceled for every rational angle by stacking a neutral, generally noninvertible Witten-Reshetikhin-Turaev layer. The same framing subtlety affects the chiral defects of QED on curved spin manifolds. The complex projective plane illustrates each of these features explicitly.
papers.summary: This paper studies how generalized global symmetries of massless QED in four dimensions are modified when the underlying spacetime is an oriented non‑spin manifold, with the photon promoted to a spin^c connection and the path integral summed over spin^c structures. It finds that the magnetic 1‑form symmetry becomes w2‑twisted, exhibits a mixed magnetic‑gravitational anomaly that can only be cancelled by summing over spin^c structures, and discusses the implications for various phases and for chiral defects, including a framing anomaly that is resolved by a non‑invertible Witten–Reshetikhin–Turaev layer.

papers.title: Are Black Hole and Cosmological Horizon Thermodynamics Necessarily Inequivalent?
papers.abstract: It has recently been argued that cosmological horizon thermodynamics and black hole thermodynamics are generically inequivalent in any consistent, UV complete theory of quantum gravity, where it was suggested that this could be falsified by the identification of a counterexample. This conjecture was motivated in part by noting that cosmological horizons do not incorporate many of the convenient features found in the black holes described by string theory. In this work, we consider as a toy model a universe with a single non-rotating black hole and a positive cosmological constant. We work in the Nariai limit where the mass of the black hole is taken to its maximum possible value, and where we also assert that the quantum field theory living on this background is strictly parity invariant. In the semi-classical regime where we neglect instability of the exact Nariai equilibrium under quantum fluctuations, we find that the observer cannot readily distinguish the physics in the neighborhood of the black hole horizon from the physics in the neighborhood of the cosmological horizon. This does not prove that the two are generically equivalent in any universe, though it does suggest that they cannot be entirely unrelated in general. We propose that any consistent theory of quantum gravity that aims to describe black holes in a universe with a positive cosmological constant should provide a related microscopic origin for the leading semiclassical cosmological entropy and black hole entropy in the neighborhood of the particular limit considered here.
papers.summary: The authors study the Nariai limit of a Schwarzschild–de Sitter black hole, showing that in a parity‑invariant semi‑classical regime the thermodynamic behavior near the black‑hole horizon mirrors that near the cosmological horizon. While this does not prove a universal equivalence, it suggests that any UV‑complete quantum‑gravity theory with a positive cosmological constant must explain both entropies from a common microscopic origin.

papers.title: Deformed Amplituhedra and Interpolating Anomalous Dimensions on the Coulomb Branch
papers.authors: Francesco Calisto, Subramanya Hegde, Mart\'in Lagares, Elia Mazzucchelli
papers.abstract: We study planar four-point scattering amplitudes on the Coulomb branch of $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills theory, focusing on multi-parameter families of massive kinematics. We extend the deformed Amplituhedron construction of \cite{Arkani-Hamed:2023epq,Flieger:2025ekn} to general external kinematics characterized by a six-parameter embedding-space Gram matrix. We show that copositivity constraints on the inverse Gram matrix control the real geometry and restrict the numerator of the two-loop canonical form to the span of the two planar double-box structures expected for the scattering amplitude. We then specialize to a three-parameter massive configuration and evaluate the relevant one- and two-loop integrals using differential equations directly in four dimensions, obtaining analytic expressions in terms of multiple polylogarithms. We investigate multiscale infrared limits of the proposed two-loop amplitude and find exponentiation through two loops. The kinematic family contains the limits governed by the cusp and octagon anomalous dimensions and interpolates between them through the walking anomalous dimension introduced in~\cite{Alday:2026cpk}. Our result reproduces the one-loop interpolation and fixes the two-loop coefficients in their proposed all-loop ansatz. Interestingly, our results suggest that the walking anomalous dimension may be entirely determined through all loop orders by the cusp and octagon anomalous dimensions.
papers.summary: The authors extend the deformed Amplituhedron framework to a six-parameter family of massive kinematics on the Coulomb branch of planar N=4 SYM, deriving two-loop canonical forms and evaluating the integrals via four-dimensional differential equations. They uncover a two-loop exponentiation pattern and show that the walking anomalous dimension interpolates between the cusp and octagon limits, fixing the two-loop coefficients of an all-loop ansatz.

papers.title: Regularized Master-Field Approximation for Mass-Deformed Supersymmetric Yang-Mills Matrix Models
papers.abstract: The regularized master-field approximation (RMA) is an efficient computational method for large-$N$ reduced matrix models, including those with multiple matrices or complex integration weights. In this work, we apply the RMA to mass-deformed supersymmetric Yang--Mills-type matrix models with three, four, and ten matrices. All three models admit fuzzy-sphere configurations as classical solutions. We show that the RMA quantitatively reproduces these fuzzy-sphere solutions and their breakdown, and that zero modes of the Dirac operator can destabilize fuzzy-sphere configurations in certain cases.
papers.summary: The paper develops a regularized master-field approximation (RMA) for large‑N mass‑deformed supersymmetric Yang–Mills matrix models with up to ten matrices, and demonstrates that it accurately reproduces fuzzy‑sphere classical solutions and their instabilities due to Dirac zero modes. This computational framework could be useful for probing non‑perturbative dynamics in matrix models that appear in holographic duals of string theory.

papers.title: virasoro_blocks: Software for the 2d bootstrap
papers.abstract: We introduce virasoro_blocks, software that computes Virasoro conformal blocks at any central charge in a form suitable for the numerical bootstrap. At each finite order in the elliptic nome, Zamolodchikov's recursion gives the block as a positive prefactor times a rational function of the exchanged weight. However, its many Kac poles make it difficult to use in semidefinite programming approaches to the bootstrap. In this software we use optimal interpolation to reduce the number of poles while keeping high accuracy. The software works in arbitrary precision and handles singular central charges, including the minimal models and $c=1$. It also computes global blocks, $N=1$ superconformal blocks, torus characters, and torus one-point blocks. We illustrate it with two applications. Assuming only scalar Virasoro primaries, we compute bounds on the scalar gap that approach the window of Liouville solutions between $(c-1)/16$ and $(c-1)/12$. We also bound the average exchanged dimension in four-point functions of identical scalars at several central charges. These bounds have a rich structure, and many known 2d CFTs lie on or near their boundary.
papers.summary: This paper presents virasoro_blocks, a high-precision computational tool for Virasoro conformal blocks at arbitrary central charge, enabling efficient numerical bootstrap analyses. Using optimal interpolation to tame Kac poles, it derives new bounds on scalar gaps and average exchanged dimensions, illuminating the spectrum of 2d CFTs including Liouville and minimal models.

papers.title: Ortho-symplectic interface line operators in $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM theories
papers.abstract: We study the line operators at the half-BPS interfaces in 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills (SYM) theories of orthogonal and symplectic gauge groups. For the NS5-type interfaces, line operators are labeled by pairs of electric or magnetic charges under the gauge groups on either side of the interface, whereas for the D5-type interfaces they are labeled by electric or magnetic charges under the single gauge group preserved by the interface. We propose dualities between the Wilson lines and vortex lines at the interfaces under the action of S-duality. As highly non-trivial evidence of the dualities on the junctions of the line operators and the interfaces, we find matching of the line defect half-indices for the dual pairs.
papers.summary: This work analyzes line operators localized on half-BPS interfaces in 4d $mathcal{N}=4$ SYM with orthogonal and symplectic gauge groups, classifying them by electric/magnetic charges on either side of the interface and proposing S-duality exchanges between Wilson and vortex lines. The authors provide nontrivial evidence by matching half-indices of dual line defect/interface configurations, offering a concrete test of the duality in this setting.

papers.title: Schwinger--Keldysh worldline effective field theory for quantum black holes: dissipation, noise and decoherence
papers.abstract: We formulate a Schwinger--Keldysh worldline effective field theory for quantum black holes that treats dissipation, fluctuations, and decoherence within one real-time influence functional. The reduced dynamics is encoded in causal response and symmetric noise kernels. Their spectra obey positivity constraints, while thermal Kubo--Martin--Schwinger symmetry relates them through the fluctuation--dissipation relation. A Hubbard--Stratonovich representation turns the noise kernel into a Gaussian source driving the resolved metric and worldline. For a leading post-Newtonian Schwarzschild binary, direct and metric-mediated stochastic forces combine into the complete relative-acceleration noise at this order, preserve center-of-mass momentum balance, and remain Planck suppressed. The same noise kernel gives the quadrupolar decoherence functional for a supported spatial superposition and reproduces the Danielson--Satishchandran--Wald horizon-induced scaling after absorptive matching. Away from thermal equilibrium, response and noise remain independent matching data. We discuss extensions to microscopic quantum structure in the worldline kernels, matching to spatially extended coarse-grained descriptions, and gravitational splitting.
papers.summary: This paper develops a Schwinger–Keldysh worldline effective field theory for quantum black holes, encoding dissipation, noise, and decoherence in a single real‑time influence functional. It applies the formalism to post‑Newtonian Schwarzschild binaries, deriving Planck‑suppressed stochastic forces and a decoherence functional that reproduces known horizon‑induced scaling.

papers.title: Quantum field theory with scale-dependent weighted measures: nonlinear momentum representations, vacuum fluctuations, and causal structure
papers.abstract: We reconsider the construction of free quantum fields through momentum-space weighted measures, introducing an independent energy scale that restores the conventional theory at low momenta. The resulting family is characterized by a dimensionless spectral function and includes, as a distinguished case, the spatial weight associated with the Euclidean Snyder algebra. We discuss its relation to modified dispersion relations and nonlinear momentum coordinates, and introduce an observer-covariant spectral weight defined using a timelike four-velocity. For the complex Klein-Gordon field we obtain the equal-time algebra, conserved weighted observables, vacuum fluctuations, and two-point functions in arbitrary spatial dimension. The ultraviolet conditions for their finiteness are established, and the nonlocal causal structure is analyzed in terms of a spatial convolution of the ordinary Pauli-Jordan distribution. An illustrative interacting extension and numerical profiles of the kernels and amplitudes are also presented.
papers.summary: This paper develops a family of quantum field theories with momentum-space weighted measures that introduce a scale-dependent spectral function, restoring standard QFT at low energies. It analyzes the resulting modified dispersion relations, vacuum fluctuations, and nonlocal causal structure, providing explicit results for the complex Klein–Gordon field and an interacting extension.

papers.title: Does SO(2,2) symmetry lead to an additional U(1) symmetry in 5-dimensional Einstein-scalar theories?
papers.abstract: Solving Einstein equations including the matter fields in dimensions higher than four is computationally challenging. However, the existence of symmetries facilitates these calculations. Among these symmetries, we can mention the SO(2,2) symmetry that arises in the near-horizon geometries of extremal black holes with vanishing horizon area in four dimensions \cite{EVH/CFT} and higher dimensions \cite{Sadeghian:2015}. Solutions of Einstein theories including scalar and Maxwell fields with SO(2,2) symmetry have been classified in four, five, and higher dimensions \cite{Sadeghian:2014}. For the Einstein-Maxwell-Lambda theory, a theorem states that SO(2,2) symmetry leads to an additional U(1) symmetry and therefore unique axisymmetric solutions. Nevertheless, in the presence of a scalar field, this symmetry group is not large enough in five dimensions to guarantee solution uniqueness, and the additional U(1) symmetry remains a conjecture in \cite{Sadeghian:2014}. Here, we study the Einstein equations of theories with a five-dimensional scalar field using the Lie symmetry method for solving partial differential equations. We challenge the conjecture in \cite{Sadeghian:2014} and find a solution that depends on both $\theta$ and $\psi$ coordinates as a counterexample to that conjecture.
papers.summary: The paper investigates whether the SO(2,2) symmetry of near‑horizon geometries in five‑dimensional Einstein–scalar theories forces an extra U(1) isometry, as conjectured for the Einstein–Maxwell–Λ case. Using Lie symmetry methods the authors construct a counterexample solution that depends on both angular coordinates, thereby refuting the conjecture.

papers.title: Absorption of bound supernova axion-like particles by the neutron star weakens the heating limits on their photon coupling
papers.authors: Probit J Kalita, Subha Mitra, Bharat Kumar
papers.abstract: Axion-like particles (ALPs) that couple to protons are produced in a core-collapse supernova, and the slow ones remain bound to the new neutron star. Bose, Ganguly, Kumar, and Raj [arXiv:2610.30255] proposed that the photons from the decay of this bound cloud reheat old neutron stars, and they derived strong limits on the ALP-photon coupling. They neglected the absorption of the ALPs by the star, but a bound ALP on an orbit that enters the star and reaches 50 km crosses it about $6\times 10^{18}$ times over the 333 Myr age of PSR J2144$-$3933. We show that inverse nucleon bremsstrahlung in the cold star absorbs every ALP whose orbit enters it within minutes, long before it decays, so only ALPs born outside the final star on nearly circular orbits survive; they carry $9\times 10^{-9} - 6\times 10^{-5}$ of the heating. We compute the protoneutron-star evolution, the production, the general-relativistic orbits and the absorption ourselves, for twelve protoneutron-star evolutions, three nucleon-bremsstrahlung rates normalized to the same supernova energy loss of light ALPs, and equations of state with and without $\Delta(1232)$ isobars. PSR J2144$-$3933 still excludes a window at $m_a\simeq 7.7-196$\ MeV, with a lower edge in the photon coupling $280-700$ times higher than without absorption. Pion conversion and the $\Delta(1232)$ resonance, which raise the production of surviving ALPs more than their absorption, widen this window to $m_a\simeq$ $7.7-260$\ MeV. The window depends at similar levels on the bremsstrahlung rate and on the radius of the final star. It requires a direct photon coupling that cancels the one induced by ALP-pion mixing, and existing supernova gamma-ray limits may already cover it.
papers.summary: The paper re‑examines constraints on axion‑like particles from neutron‑star heating by including absorption via inverse nucleon bremsstrahlung, finding that only a tiny fraction of bound ALPs survive to decay and thus weakening earlier bounds on the ALP‑photon coupling. Detailed protoneutron‑star evolution, orbit calculations, and absorption modeling across various equations of state show the allowed mass window shifts and may already be excluded by gamma‑ray limits.

papers.title: Carrollian CFTs and the Light Front
papers.authors: Arjun Bagchi, Kinjal Banerjee, Sourish Banerjee, Meghaa AK
papers.abstract: Carrollian symmetries play an important role in building holographic duals to asymptotically flat spacetimes (AFS). This construction hinges on the isomorphism between the (asymptotic) isometries of AFS and the conformal Carroll algebra. Carroll symmetries also naturally arise on the lightfront, as co-dimension one subalgebras in the Poincare algebra written in lightcone coordinates. In this paper, building on the isomorphism between four dimensional (4d) Poincare and 3d conformal Carroll algebras, we make a connection between physics on the lightfront and Carrollian CFTs. Using insights from the lightfront literature, we construct new representations of Carroll CFTs that connect to massive bulk scattering. We compute two-point functions and build a map between 3d Carroll CFTs and 4d lightfront theories living in AFS.
papers.summary: This work establishes a concrete link between 3d Carrollian CFTs and 4d lightfront theories in asymptotically flat spacetimes by exploiting the isomorphism between the 4d Poincaré algebra and the 3d conformal Carroll algebra. It introduces new Carrollian representations that encode massive bulk scattering, computes two‑point functions, and provides a dictionary mapping between Carrollian correlators and lightfront observables.

papers.title: Large-$N$ limit of chiral quiver theories: free energy, supersymmetric indices and operator counting
papers.authors: Edoardo Colombo, Hyojoong Kim, Nakwoo Kim, Hoseob Shin
papers.abstract: We find the first analytic solution to the large-$N$ saddle point equations for the $S^3$ free energy of a chiral $\mathcal N=2$ Chern-Simons-matter theory with an M-theory dual. Focusing on the chiral quiver dual to AdS$_4\times Q^{1,1,1}/\mathbb Z_{\rm k}$, we show how the long-range forces of the matrix model cancel at large $N$, resolving a long-standing tension with the expected $N^{3/2}$ scaling. The resulting free energy precisely matches the holographic prediction for all assignments of trial R-charges. Our results extend to the superconformal and topologically twisted indices on $S^2\times S^1$, whose large-$N$ and Cardy limit is determined by the same saddle. The solution agrees with the predictions of the operator counting method, giving strong evidence for this conjecture beyond non-chiral quivers. We support the analytic solution with a finite-$N$ numerical analysis for multiple assignments of R-charges, extending recent numerical results obtained for this quiver.
papers.summary: The authors solve the large‑N saddle point equations for the S^3 free energy of a chiral N=2 Chern‑Simons‑matter quiver dual to AdS4×Q^{1,1,1}/Z_k, showing that long‑range forces cancel and yielding the expected N^{3/2} scaling that matches the holographic prediction for arbitrary trial R‑charges. They extend the solution to the superconformal and topologically twisted indices on S^2×S^1, confirm the operator‑counting conjecture for chiral quivers, and support the analytic results with finite‑N numerics.

papers.title: Superstring Field Theory with Double Background Independence
papers.abstract: A recently constructed superstring field theory has two decoupled sectors, the physical superstring and a shadow sector with a second copy of the superstring. These are both expanded around the same background conformal field theory and the theory is independent of marginal deformations of this common background. A form of the action is presented that is symmetric between the two sectors. A generalisation of this theory is given in which the two sectors can be expanded around two different backgrounds, and the theory is independent under separate marginal deformations of the two background conformal field theories.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a superstring field theory featuring two decoupled sectors—one physical and one shadow—both expanded around the same background CFT, with an action symmetric between them and invariant under marginal deformations. It further generalizes to allow the two sectors to be expanded around distinct backgrounds, maintaining separate background independence.

papers.title: Majorana Neutrino Physics and Matter-Antimatter Asymmetry in Type IIA String Theory
papers.abstract: We study Majorana neutrino masses and the matter-antimatter asymmetry in Type IIA string theory on a $T^6/(\mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_2)$ orientifold with intersecting D6-branes. Euclidean D2-instantons with $\text{Sp}(2)$ Chan-Paton symmetry generate both the seesaw mechanism and the Weinberg operator. The flavour vectors are not computed from a compactification but fixed by matching, so our results are an existence proof. Matching the measured mass-squared differences selects the seesaw-dominated case with normal ordering. Swampland criteria constrain the instanton action and the reheating temperature. A benchmark example reproduces the neutrino parameters, gives $\eta_B \approx 8.6 \times 10^{-11}$, within an order of magnitude of observation, and predicts $\langle m_{\beta \beta} \rangle =2.594 \text{meV}$. A parameter scan shows the mass hierarchy is accommodated rather than predicted.
papers.summary: This paper constructs a Type IIA orientifold with intersecting D6-branes where Euclidean D2-instantons generate Majorana neutrino masses via the seesaw mechanism and the Weinberg operator. It shows that a benchmark model can reproduce neutrino oscillation data and generate the observed baryon asymmetry while satisfying swampland constraints, but does not predict the neutrino mass hierarchy.

papers.title: On functional classes in higher-spin theory
papers.abstract: The factorization over the ideal in the $d$-dimensional Vasiliev theory requires an accurate description of the higher-spin algebra $\mathcal{A}$ and its twisted adjoint module $\mathcal{A}^{tw}$ as certain functional spaces. It is shown that the conditions of $\mathcal{A}$ to be closed under action of the Moyal star product, and of $\mathcal{A}^{tw}$ to be a star-product $\mathcal{A}$-module along with some auxiliary conditions lead to properly defined free-level factorization procedure. The conditions on admissible functions have simple algebraic form; in the case of $\mathcal{A}$ the analogous functional space has been considered by Soloviev \cite{Soloviev:2013iba}. The relation of the obtained functional classes to the locality problem in the Vasiliev theory is discussed. In particular it is observed that certain non-local expressions diverge due to properties of $\mathcal{A}^{tw}$ while the spin-local expressions are well-defined.
papers.summary: The paper develops precise functional spaces for the higher-spin algebra and its twisted module in Vasiliev theory, enabling a consistent factorization of the equations of motion at the free level. It shows that certain non‑local terms diverge while spin‑local expressions remain well‑defined, offering insights into the locality problem in higher‑spin holography.

papers.title: Initial conditions leave IR imprints in quantum cosmology
papers.authors: Manishankar Ailiga, Akash Mondal, Gaurav Narain
papers.abstract: We investigate the gravitational path integral of $\mathbb{R} \times S^3$ geometries in Lorentzian signature along with the metric fluctuations which live on the $S^3$ hypersurfaces. Each metric configuration is characterised by lapse, scale factor and fluctuations, and is weighted by the exponential of the Einstein-Hilbert action. A particular boundary requirement for the scale-factor is achievable via an infinite family of covariant boundary actions, each restricting the boundary behaviour of the fluctuation field which cannot be arbitrarily chosen. The paper explores the effect of this infinite family of covariant boundary actions on the wavefunction of Universe to one-loop. These boundary actions are characterized by parameters $c$ and $\omega$. Dominant contribution of initial momentum in the path-integral restricts $\omega$ to be half-integer, leading to an infinite family of $c$-dependent conjugate momenta. In special case for fixed $\omega$, four such $c$-dependent dominant branches of conjugate momenta emerge: two lead to deSitter, one leads to Hartle-Hawking and one to the tunnelling Universe. For all these $c$-dependent initial conjugate momenta, the lapse-saddles are relevant, however only, one of deSitter saddle and Hartle Hawking saddle have well-behaved perturbations. The one-loop wavefunction at these well-behaved saddles is computed systematically by isolating the UV-divergences, where the covariant boundary parameter $c$ acts as a UV-regulator and also helps in shifting the poles of one-loop determinant, away from the real $q_f$ axis for dS saddles, where $q_f$ is the final size of the Universe. UV-finite wavefunction for no-boundary and dS is obtained by adding suitable counterterms. The infrared behaviour of these wavefunctions show not only IR-divergences but also sensitivity toward the initial boundary choices.
papers.summary: This paper studies the Lorentzian path integral for $mathbb{R}	imes S^3$ geometries, including metric fluctuations, and shows that a family of covariant boundary actions parametrized by $c$ and $omega$ determines the initial conjugate momenta and selects de Sitter, Hartle–Hawking, or tunnelling saddle points. The authors compute the one‑loop wavefunction, regularize UV divergences with the boundary parameter, and find that the resulting infrared behaviour depends sensitively on the initial boundary choice.

papers.title: The Effective Kerr-Compton Tree Amplitude from Black Hole Perturbation Theory
papers.authors: N. Emil J. Bjerrum-Bohr, Gang Chen, Konstantinos Papadimos, Nabha Shah, Chenliang Su
papers.abstract: We develop a new method to construct the tree-level Compton amplitude for gravitational-wave scattering off a Kerr black hole in post-Minkowskian effective field theory. Building on previous computations that required physical consistency of the amplitude, the method uses wave scattering functions from black hole perturbation theory to uniquely determine additional contact terms. We illustrate the iterative procedure by deriving explicit expressions up to sixth order in spin, including previously unknown sectors at the fifth and sixth orders in spin. The amplitude features complex transcendental structures and a leading dissipative contact term at sixth order in spin. We verify our result against known results in the literature and reproduce the one-loop tail result from black hole perturbation theory.
papers.summary: This paper presents a new method to compute the tree-level Compton amplitude for gravitational-wave scattering off a Kerr black hole using black hole perturbation theory and post-Minkowskian effective field theory. It derives explicit spin-dependent contact terms up to sixth order, revealing complex transcendental structures and a dissipative term, and reproduces known one-loop tail results.

papers.title: $\mathcal{N}=4$ Super Yang-Mills Flux Tube in AdS
papers.authors: Victor Gorbenko, Orr Sela, Brian R. Zielazienski
papers.abstract: We study a supersymmetric Wilson line on the boundary of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory in AdS$_4$, or equivalently on a half-space, as a model for exploring the connection between holographic strings and confining flux tubes. The boundary breaks four-dimensional conformal symmetry and is expected to remove integrability, bringing this system closer to a confining string while preserving enough supersymmetry to constrain its dynamics. Working in the planar limit, we analyze the defect spectrum at weak and strong coupling and compute the superconformal index, thereby relating the perturbative gauge-theory description to the worldsheet excitations of a long holographic string. These complementary perspectives allow us to propose a map between operators in the two regimes, under which the worldsheet axion, in particular, becomes a two-particle state at strong coupling. The resulting picture supports a smooth interpolation from an exponentially growing gauge-theory spectrum to the Cardy-like spectrum of a string worldsheet, providing a non-integrable supersymmetric model for investigating the spectral reorganization expected in confining gauge theories.
papers.summary: The paper studies a supersymmetric Wilson line defect in planar N=4 SYM on AdS4, analyzing its defect spectrum and superconformal index to relate weak‑coupling gauge theory operators to long‑string worldsheet excitations, including a mapping of the worldsheet axion to a two‑particle state at strong coupling. This provides a non‑integrable, supersymmetric holographic model that interpolates between an exponentially growing gauge‑theory spectrum and a Cardy‑like string spectrum, offering a new laboratory for exploring spectral reorganization in confining gauge theories.

papers.title: A density calculus for quantum field theory
papers.abstract: These notes provide an introduction to Haagerup noncommutative $L^p$ spaces for quantum field theorists. The aim is to explain how the familiar calculus of density matrices, fractional powers, and Schatten norms extends to local observable algebras of type~III, where an intrinsic trace is unavailable. We develop the construction first for a matrix algebra, making the crossed product, its trace, and the dual action explicit, before passing to general von Neumann algebras. Particular attention is paid to the representation of normal states by Haagerup densities and to the distinction between the crossed-product trace and the canonical Haagerup functional used to compute expectation values. As a concrete application, we calculate the sandwiched R\'enyi divergence for a coherent excitation of a chiral current, verifying monotonicity under restriction and the R\'enyi quantum null energy condition at every real order $\alpha>1$. The presentation assumes familiarity with quantum mechanics and elementary quantum field theory, while introducing the operator-algebraic concepts needed for the construction and calculation.
papers.summary: This paper develops Haagerup noncommutative (L^p) spaces to extend density-matrix calculus to type III local algebras, providing explicit constructions via crossed products and computing sandwiched Rényi divergences for chiral current excitations. It demonstrates monotonicity and the Rényi quantum null energy condition for all real (alpha>1), offering a rigorous operator-algebraic framework for quantum field theoretic density matrices.

papers.title: Quantum curves of 6d SCFTs on a -3 curve
papers.authors: Minsung Kim, Sung-Soo Kim, Xin Wang
papers.abstract: We study half-BPS defects and quantum Seiberg-Witten curves in 6d $ \mathcal{N}=(1,0) $ SCFTs on a $ -3 $ curve. We compute the partition functions in the presence of codimension-4 and codimension-2 defects on $ \mathbb{R}^4 \times T^2 $ using generalized blowup equations. We then propose quantum Seiberg-Witten curves as elliptic difference equations satisfied by the Nekrasov-Shatashvili limits of the defect partition functions. We apply this construction to the minimal $ \mathfrak{su}(3) $ gauge theory, and to the $ \mathfrak{g}_2 $ and $ \mathfrak{so}(N) $ gauge theories on a Higgsing tree whose endpoint is the minimal $ \mathfrak{su}(3) $ theory. We also investigate defects and the quantum curve of the $ \mathfrak{su}(3) $ gauge theory compactified on a circle with a $ \mathbb{Z}_2 $ twist.
papers.summary: This paper constructs quantum Seiberg-Witten curves for 6d (1,0) SCFTs on a -3 curve by computing defect partition functions via blowup equations and proposes elliptic difference equations for their Nekrasov-Shatashvili limits. It applies the framework to minimal su(3), g2, so(N) theories and explores a Z2-twisted su(3) compactification.

papers.title: Competition and coexistence of baryonic condensates in AdS hardwall model
papers.abstract: Cold dense QCD admits several order parameters for baryon-number breaking, among them diquark and dibaryon condensates. We ask whether they exclude one another or coexist, using a five-dimensional AdS hardwall model with full backreaction in which two charged scalars, dual to operators of charges $q_i$ and dimensions $\Delta_i$, couple to a common $U(1)_B$ gauge field. With the diquark-like operator fixed at $q_1=2$, $\Delta_1=3$, both operators condense only within a narrow window of $\Delta_2$, which widens with $q_2$ and closes when the operators coincide. Outside the window, only a single condensate forms. The structure persists in both confined and deconfined phases. In the $\mu_B$-$T$ plane, confined matter with both condensates is preferred at low temperature, below a narrow band of deconfined matter with one condensate.
papers.summary: The study explores how diquark and dibaryon condensates compete or coexist in a backreacted AdS hardwall setup, revealing a narrow window of simultaneous condensation that depends on operator dimensions and charges. The phase diagram shows confined matter with dual condensates favored at low temperature, while deconfined phases support only one condensate outside the window.

papers.title: $\mathcal{N}=2$ conformal higher-spin actions in harmonic superspace
papers.abstract: We construct linearized $4D, \mathcal{N}=2$ Weyl-type off-shell actions in harmonic superspace for the superconformal higher-spin gauge multiplets introduced in arXiv:2404.19016. This work is a followup of our arXiv:2511.16325, where an analogous construction was carried out for conformal $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity. We check the superconformal invariance of the new actions and their linearized gauge invariance. As the characteristic features of our formulation, the structure of the underlying prepotentials and their gauge and superconformal transformations are entirely determined by the fundamental \textit{principle of Grassmann harmonic analyticity}, while the construction of the invariant actions and of the generalized $\mathcal{N}=2$ super-Weyl tensors relies upon the \textit{principle of Grassmann half-analyticity}. This provides not only a new geometric framework for the linearized $\mathcal{N}=2$ superconformal gauge higher-spin theories, but also suggests possible ways of promoting them to the full nonlinear level. We consider a generalization to an arbitrary $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity background and show that the linearized spin-$\mathbf{s}$ gauge invariance, without radical modifications of the gauge transformation law and/or harmonic zero-curvature equations, is consistent only with $\mathcal{N}=2$ Weyl-flat super-backgrounds.
papers.summary: This paper constructs linearized Ó=2 Weyl-type actions for superconformal higher‑spin gauge multiplets in harmonic superspace, verifying superconformal and gauge invariance. The framework relies on Grassmann harmonic analyticity and suggests extensions to nonlinear regimes and constraints on supergravity backgrounds.

papers.title: Bounds on the Diagonal Degree of the Biadjoint Scalar Amplitude Matrix
papers.abstract: Biadjoint scalar theory partial amplitudes, $m_n(\alpha,\beta)$, define an $(n-1)!/2\times (n-1)!/2$ matrix, $M_n$, with rows and columns labeled by orderings. The CHY construction of $M_n$ implies that its rank is $(n-3)!$. Invertible submatrices of maximal rank enter in the KLT construction relating graviton amplitudes to gluon amplitudes. Motivated by finding the KLT formula with the smallest number of terms, one of the authors posed the question of whether there is a critical $n_c$ such that for all $n>n_c$ there exists a diagonal submatrix of $M_n$ of rank $(n-3)!$. In this work we obtain bounds on the size of the largest non-singular diagonal submatrix of $M_n$, which we call its diagonal degree $\Delta_n$, and we answer the question in the negative. We prove that the diagonal degree is exponentially suppressed relative to the CHY rank: $\Delta_n/(n-3)! = \exp(-\Theta (n))$ as $n\to \infty$. More explicitly, we establish the bounds $\exp(-1.5n)\leq\Delta_n/(n-3)!\leq \exp \left[ -0.01n+O(1)\right]$.
papers.summary: The paper studies the rank structure of the biadjoint scalar amplitude matrix M_n, showing that its diagonal submatrices of maximal rank are exponentially rare, disproving a conjecture that such submatrices exist for all sufficiently large n. It establishes explicit exponential bounds on the diagonal degree Δ_n relative to the CHY rank (n-3)!.

papers.title: Exact holographic superfluid at the Bogomolny point: transport, large charge, and R\'enyi entropies
