papers.abstract: The Abelian Higgs model in AdS$_5$, in the probe limit, is a standard holographic model of a strongly coupled superfluid, usually solved numerically. When the scalar mass saturates the Breitenlohner-Freedman bound and the quartic coupling takes the Bogomolny value, its condensed phase can be found in closed form on every static, uncharged AdS$_5$ background with maximally symmetric spatial sections. We prove that it is linearly stable, as is any nodeless probe-limit condensate in the standard quantization with a nonnegative quartic coupling and no superflow. On each slicing it answers a different question about the dual conformal field theory. On the planar black brane it is the superfluid at all temperatures below $T_c$: the superfluid fraction follows the Gorter-Casimir two-fluid law exactly, and the speed and the attenuation of sound are found in closed form. In global AdS$_5$ it describes a state of charge $Q$ on $\mathbb{R}\times S^3$, arguably the lowest-energy one, and gives its scaling dimension in closed form at all $Q$, classically in the bulk. Its excitations include towers that the superfluid effective theory does not describe; they come from an infrared fixed point of the probe sector. The hyperbolic slicing gives in closed form a homogeneous hairy phase of the black holes that compute the charged R\'enyi entropies of a ball. Its condensate does not vanish at the entangling surface. When sourced by operators inserted there, the phase sets in at R\'enyi index exactly one at zero chemical potential, as found for a neutral scalar.
papers.summary: The authors solve the Abelian Higgs model at the Breitenlohner–Freedman bound and Bogomolny coupling in closed form on any static, uncharged AdS$_5$ slicing, yielding analytic expressions for the superfluid phase, its transport coefficients, large‑charge spectrum, and charged Rényi entropies. This provides a rare analytic benchmark for holographic superfluids, revealing exact two‑fluid behavior, infrared fixed‑point excitations, and a non‑vanishing condensate at entangling surfaces.

papers.title: Breaking of integrability in elliptic deformations of AdS3 strings with mixed flux
papers.authors: Ian Le Meur, Fiona K. Seibold
papers.abstract: We construct elliptic deformations of the $AdS_3 \times S^3 \times T^4$ superstring supported by mixed NSNS and RR fluxes in type IIB supergravity and investigate their integrability. The NSNS sector includes a Wess-Zumino term, and imposing that the theory preserves 8 supersymmetries also requires the presence of a B-field coupling the deformed $AdS_3$ and $S^3$ factors. We explore integrability from two different perspectives: through the construction of a flat Lax connection and the computation of the tree-level worldsheet S-matrix. For generic elliptic parameters and NSNS flux, we find inelastic $2 \rightarrow 2$ amplitudes, violating the elasticity required by integrability. In the integrable cases as identified by the Lax analysis, these inelastic amplitudes vanish and the tree-level S-matrix satisfies the classical Yang-Baxter equation. In particular, the addition of a Wess-Zumino term, which preserves integrability in the rational and trigonometric models, breaks integrability for elliptic deformations.
papers.summary: This paper constructs elliptic deformations of the AdS3×S3×T4 superstring with mixed NSNS/RR fluxes and studies their integrability via a Lax connection and tree‑level S‑matrix. It finds that generic elliptic parameters break integrability, while special cases preserve it, with the Wess‑Zumino term destroying integrability in the elliptic setting.

papers.title: Holographic duals of JT gravity at finite cutoff: the classical case
papers.authors: Andreas Belaey, Thomas G. Mertens, Lorenzo Russo, Alex Tarana
papers.abstract: We formulate JT gravity with finite-cutoff boundaries and end-of-the-world branes in the first-order BF formulation. We dynamically reduce the BF model into a one-dimensional system living at the boundaries, generalizing earlier constructions. We obtain in particular a geometrical understanding of the phase space degrees of freedom associated to each of these boundaries. We leverage these results to probe bulk locality and the underlying structure of spacetime. Within our framework, we are able to derive a closed-form expression for the holographic Schwarzian description of JT gravity at finite-cutoff in phase space. The resulting degrees of freedom describe the embedding of the finite-cutoff curve in AdS$_2$. A quantization of these systems is presented in a companion paper.
papers.summary: This work reformulates JT gravity with finite-cutoff boundaries and end-of-the-world branes in a first-order BF language, reducing the bulk theory to a one-dimensional boundary system that captures the phase space of each boundary. The authors derive a closed-form holographic Schwarzian action describing the embedding of the finite-cutoff curve in AdS$_2$, providing a new geometric perspective on bulk locality.

papers.title: A Simplified Born Rule for Cosmological Correlators
papers.abstract: Cosmological correlators are natural observables of the primordial universe and are related to wavefunction coefficients by the Born rule. For equal-time in-in correlators in flat spacetime, we prove that all double-boundary poles cancel for arbitrary graphs, including in theories with local derivative interactions. These cancellations occur before integration over spatial loop momenta and yield a $\textit{simplified Born rule}$ in terms of what we call embedded wavefunction coefficients. The resulting expansion reveals which physical poles can occur together while keeping the interaction dependence explicit. For conformally coupled $\operatorname{Tr}(\phi^3)$ theory in flat spacetime, the simplified Born rule takes the form of a uniformly weighted forest-cut expansion. From its pole combinatorics, we construct what we call the $\textit{Born polytope}$, whose canonical function reproduces the normalized correlator for arbitrary graphs after matching its facet supports to the physical energies. The same geometry also yields a stringy formula for correlators.
papers.summary: The authors derive a simplified Born rule that expresses equal‑time in‑in cosmological correlators directly in terms of embedded wavefunction coefficients, showing that all double‑boundary poles cancel before spatial loop integration. They further introduce a Born polytope whose canonical function reproduces the normalized correlator for arbitrary graphs, offering a new geometric and stringy perspective on cosmological observables.

papers.title: Gravity between two masses beyond Newton's law
papers.abstract: Newton's law of universal gravitation describes the attraction between two masses through an inverse-distance potential. In Einstein's theory gravity gravitates: each mass reshapes the spacetime geometry through which the other acts. More than a century later, extracting the two-body interaction from this coupled geometry remains a fundamental analytical challenge. Even without motion or radiation, the static sector of the interaction harbours an infinite hierarchy of field couplings: the purest laboratory for gravitational non-linearity. Here we determine the static interaction from ninth to twelfth order in Newton's constant for arbitrary mass ratios, and derive a closed expression for the first backreaction beyond the Schwarzschild test-body limit to all orders in the gravitational coupling. We achieve both advances by formulating the problem around the stationary interaction energy. An exact one-body background resums one source's self-interaction, stationarity reduces the fields required from the other, and integrated response identities reveal cancellations across the coupled modes. Complementary expansions then resolve the complete mass dependence at finite order. Together, these results bridge the gap between an infinitesimal probe and comparable masses, exposing hidden analytical simplicity within Einstein's theory and providing essential building blocks for modelling orbital dynamics and gravitational-wave generation.
papers.summary: The paper computes the static gravitational interaction between two masses to ninth through twelfth order in Newton's constant, providing a closed‑form expression for the first backreaction beyond the test‑body limit. These results offer new analytic tools for modeling comparable‑mass binary dynamics and gravitational‑wave generation.

papers.title: Generalised $\Omega$-backgrounds in twisted $N=4$ super Yang-Mills
papers.abstract: We introduce rigid supergravity backgrounds for 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills which deform its topological twists and generalise the $\Omega$-deformation of $\mathcal{N}=2$ gauge theories. We derive the twisted supersymmetry variations of the $\mathcal{N}=4$ Weyl multiplet, and the $\mathcal{N}=4$ matter multiplet coupled to a rigid bosonic background, for each of the three inequivalent topological twists. Other, more exotic backgrounds are also discussed.
papers.summary: This paper constructs rigid supergravity backgrounds that deform the topological twists of four‑dimensional N=4 super Yang–Mills, extending the Ω‑deformation familiar from N=2 theories. The authors derive the twisted supersymmetry variations for the N=4 Weyl and matter multiplets in each of the three inequivalent twists, and discuss additional exotic backgrounds.

papers.title: Localization in Seven-Dimensional Supergravity
papers.abstract: Seven-dimensional supergravity provides holographic access to strongly coupled six-dimensional superconformal theories through its highest-dimensional supersymmetric AdS vacua. Its unique spinor-bilinear geometry and massive higher-form dynamics make systematic analysis and solution-finding distinctively challenging. Relative equivariant localization can obtain supersymmetric observables in odd dimensions from fixed-point data on an auxiliary even-dimensional filling, without an explicit solution. We extend this approach to seven dimensions in maximal Cartan-gauged supergravity with all gauge fields active. We formulate the Euclidean action and Killing-spinor equations in terms of field strengths, and construct a bilinear system adapted to the change in spinor reality conditions from symplectic-Majorana to Majorana. On the non-null gauged active spinor branch, independent, oppositely R-charged spinors are paired by Majorana conjugation on the same complex background. One algebraic gauging correction and two algebraic bilinear projections suffice to extend the equal-charge sector to independent Cartan charges, and the underlying efficient reorganization also applies in the Lorentzian theory. Massive 3-form self-duality fixes the quartic anomaly class and determines the higher-form fixed-point datum from Abelian moment maps. Localization at the single fixed point of the filling recovers the general supersymmetric AdS$_7$ black-hole action, without extending the solution. We prove gauge-covariant Killing-spinor invariance under the combined supersymmetric Killing flow and R-symmetry action, deriving the linear chemical-potential constraint. Extremizing the constrained entropy functional and requiring real positive stationary entropy yields the nonlinear charge relation within the Euclidean analysis, equivalent to Lorentzian horizon extremality for the known spherical black-hole family.
papers.summary: The paper develops a relative equivariant localization framework for seven‑dimensional maximal supergravity, enabling the computation of supersymmetric observables—including the AdS$_7$ black‑hole action—without solving the full equations of motion. It reformulates the Euclidean action and Killing‑spinor equations in terms of field strengths, handles the spinor reality change from symplectic‑Majorana to Majorana, and derives a chemical‑potential constraint that reproduces known horizon extremality conditions.

papers.title: Thermodynamics of Swirling Black Holes and Kerr-Taub-NUT
papers.authors: Ernesto Frodden, Diego Hidalgo, Francisco Manzano
papers.abstract: We establish the first law of black hole thermodynamics for the recently discovered Kerr swirling (KS) and accelerated Kerr swirling (AKS) black hole solutions. We also revisit the first law for the Kerr-Taub-NUT (KTN) spacetime. Guided by Noether's original insight that global symmetries give rise to conservation laws, we employ and adapt the surface charge method for computing the associated charges (mass and angular momentum) in the presence of spacetime string-like defects (conical singularities) along the axes of both KS and KTN black holes. We obtain finite integrated charges in a quasi-local manner, without relying on the non-flat asymptotic regions characteristic of these spacetimes. We then establish a first law without introducing independent stringy terms unrelated to symmetries. For both KS and KTN, the quantities that play the role of the black hole entropy differ from the simple geometrical rule of one-fourth of the horizon area. This mismatch arises because we keep first-law charges associated with conservation laws. It indicates that standard formulas may not be naively used for black holes with string-like defects; they have a different topology and suggest the need for a new geometrical framework. In stark contrast, for the AKS spacetime, which can be regularized outside the singularity and lacks string-like defects, we find that the charges are consistent with a first law having the usual one-fourth of the area entropy. We first determine the mass using the Christodoulou-Ruffini formula and then check its agreement with the result obtained from the surface charge method.
papers.summary: The authors derive a consistent first law for Kerr swirling and Kerr–Taub–NUT black holes using a surface charge approach that accounts for conical singularities, finding that the entropy deviates from the usual area law. For the regularized accelerated Kerr swirling case, the standard area‑entropy relation is recovered and the mass matches the Christodoulou–Ruffini formula.

papers.title: On Geometric Observables in Gravity
papers.authors: Manthos Karydas, Murat Kologlu, Allic Sivaramakrishnan
papers.abstract: Measures of geometry like distance and time are staples of classical gravity. While geometric quantities arise broadly in quantum gravity, their graviton corrections are less explored. In this paper, we study geometric observables in perturbative quantum gravity. We form distance and time observables that model measurements, including in the presence of spacetime fluctuations. Gravitational dressing ensures these constructions are coordinate invariant. Then we show how these finite-distance observables become memory and Shapiro time delay operators upon taking asymptotic limits. We compute leading graviton effects in correlators of geometric observables throughout. Altogether, our results identify a class of geometric observables that link experiments and operations on the celestial sphere.
papers.summary: This paper constructs coordinate-invariant distance and time observables in perturbative quantum gravity, incorporating gravitational dressing to model measurements amid spacetime fluctuations. It demonstrates that these finite-distance observables reduce to memory and Shapiro time delay operators at asymptotic infinity, computing leading graviton corrections and connecting experimental observables to celestial sphere operations.

papers.title: Generalized Dirac Equation in Metric-Affine Spacetimes: Consistency, Effective Mass, and Spinor Curvature
papers.authors: Muzaffer Adak, Ali Bagci, Caglar Pala, Ozcan Sert
papers.abstract: We formulate a generalized Dirac equation in four-dimensional metric-affine spacetimes with curvature, torsion, and non-metricity. The spinor connection is expanded over the complete basis of the Clifford algebra $cl(1,3)$ and contains eight complex coupling constants. Requiring agreement between direct covariantization of the Dirac equation and variation of the corresponding symmetrized Lagrangian imposes eight real consistency conditions, reducing the number of independent real parameters from sixteen to eight. In the static isotropic symmetric teleparallel sector, formal Hermiticity of the Hamiltonian with respect to the curved-space Dirac inner product reproduces the corresponding restrictions on the non-metricity and coframe couplings. The coframe-dependent terms introduce scalar and pseudoscalar mass contributions that persist in Minkowski spacetime. For a single free Dirac field with constant coefficients, they yield one effective mass, $m_{\mathrm{eff}}=\sqrt{(m-4b_3)^2+16b_4^2}$, and a chiral phase removable by a constant chiral field redefinition. A nonzero effective mass is therefore possible even when the original mass parameter vanishes. We also derive the Clifford decomposition of the generalized spinor curvature and show that it can remain nonzero when affine curvature, torsion, and non-metricity all vanish. When $m=0$, the combination $b_3^2+b_4^2$ determines both the effective mass squared and the surviving spinor curvature, establishing an algebraic link between these contributions.
papers.summary: The paper develops a fully consistent generalized Dirac equation in metric‑affine spacetimes, deriving eight real consistency conditions that reduce the parameter space from sixteen to eight. It shows that coframe couplings generate scalar and pseudoscalar mass terms, yielding an effective mass even for a massless Dirac field, and that spinor curvature can survive when affine curvature, torsion, and non‑metricity vanish.

papers.title: Validity Domains for Semiclassical Time in Quantum Cosmology
papers.abstract: We investigate the domain in which a semiclassical gravitational WKB flow can serve as a quantitatively controlled temporal reference for subordinate quantum degrees of freedom. Rather than introducing WKB time at the outset, we formulate the Born--Oppenheimer adiabatic condition directly on gravitational configuration space using the Hamilton--Jacobi vector field. This separates adiabatic control from the local WKB validity of the gravitational branch and from the sharpness of the candidate reference against quantum fluctuations. For a single selected semiclassical branch, these requirements define the validity domain $D_t = D_{\mathrm{WKB}} \cap D_{\mathrm{ad}} \cap D_{\mathrm{sharp}}$, with an additional decoherence condition when coherent branches coexist.In a closed Friedmann--Robertson--Walker minisuperspace coupled to a homogeneous massive scalar mode, the distinction is explicit: approaching the gravitational turning point from the oscillatory region, the ordinary WKB control parameter diverges while the configuration-space adiabatic parameter tends to zero. A uniform Airy treatment of the turning point removes the formal WKB divergence while preserving the inequivalence: the corresponding local control parameter remains of order unity, whereas the configuration-space adiabatic parameter is parametrically suppressed as $O(M^{-1/3})$.Thus Born--Oppenheimer adiabaticity and gravitational WKB validity define inequivalent domains even within the simplest minisuperspace model. We conclude that the existence of an oscillatory semiclassical branch is not sufficient for a reliable WKB temporal description: semiclassical temporal reliability is instead determined by the overlap of the validity domains supporting the reference flow.
papers.summary: This paper investigates when a semiclassical WKB gravitational flow can be used as a reliable time variable for quantum fields in cosmology. It shows that WKB validity, Born–Oppenheimer adiabaticity, and decoherence define distinct domains, and that near a turning point the adiabatic parameter remains small while the WKB control parameter diverges, implying that an oscillatory branch alone is insufficient for a trustworthy semiclassical time.

papers.title: Draining Without Emptying a Stringy Black Hole: Repetitive Electric Penrose Process
papers.authors: Huai-Fan Li, Xiong-Ying Guo, Ke Wang, Hong Lei
papers.abstract: This paper studies the repetitive electric Penrose process in the Gibbons-Maeda-Garfinkle-Horowitz-Strominger (GMGHS) black hole under the optimal condition for maximum energy extraction. Unlike the Reissner-Nordstr\"om (RN) black hole, the effective potential curve of the incident particle in the GMGHS black hole remains unchanged during the iterations. The iteration termination conditions are determined by two aspects: the escape condition requires that particle 0 can overcome the effective potential peak and escape to infinity, and this condition is independent of the black hole charge; the existence condition for negative-energy particle 1 requires the black hole charge to be sufficiently large, indicating that the repetitive process cannot completely consume the charge of the GMGHS black hole to zero. Numerical simulations show that the return on investment of energy extraction can exceed $100\%$, but the energy utilization efficiency does not exceed $50\%$, and most of the extractable energy is converted into an increase in the irreducible mass of the black hole. In addition, a smaller decay radius and a larger absolute value of the charge-to-mass ratio of particle 1 can improve the return on investment and energy utilization efficiency of energy extraction; the larger the specific energy of the incident particle, the smaller the return on investment of energy extraction, while the energy utilization efficiency remains unchanged; for an initially non-extremal black hole, as the initial charge increases, the return on investment of energy extraction increases monotonically, while the energy utilization efficiency first increases and then decreases. After the iterations end, the black hole still retains extractable energy, and neither the charge nor the mass vanishes.
papers.summary: The paper investigates repeated electric Penrose processes in GMGHS black holes, showing that the effective potential remains unchanged across iterations and that the process cannot fully deplete the black hole's charge. Numerical results indicate energy extraction efficiencies up to 50% and returns exceeding 100%, but most energy goes into increasing the black hole's irreducible mass.

papers.title: Circular Axion String Loop Simulations: Field Theory and Effective Description
papers.authors: Mathieu Kaltschmidt, Javier Redondo, Ivan Rybak, Kenichi Saikawa, Iker Sanz-Gonz\'alez
papers.abstract: An accurate description of axion strings and their radiation is crucial for understanding their cosmological implications. Motivated by the differing conclusions of previous works, we study a simple, controlled setup: the collapse of an initially static circular loop in a Minkowski background. We compare field-theory simulations of the conventional complex scalar and high-tension Klaer--Moore models with solutions of the renormalised Nambu--Goto--Kalb--Ramond (NGKR) equation of motion, covering the range $3 \lesssim \mathcal{T} \lesssim 100$ in dimensionless string tension. Both the field theory and NGKR approach the Nambu--Goto (NG) limit with corrections scaling as $1/\mathcal{T}$. However, the leading correction to the halving-time is $20-35\%$ larger in NGKR than in the field-theory simulations over the same range of tensions, while for large tensions the value agrees with an independent perturbative calculation to $0.2\%$. The late-time axion spectrum agrees with NGKR in the infrared, but the collapse generates additional structure in the ultraviolet part of the spectrum, which we attribute to different events such as an outgoing wave front that carries a sizable fraction of the energy or the rebound of the initial loop. These results provide a useful benchmark for a more accurate understanding of axion radiation from cosmological string networks.
papers.summary: This study simulates the collapse of a circular axion string loop in Minkowski space, comparing field‑theory results with the renormalised Nambu–Goto–Kalb–Ramond (NGKR) effective description across a range of string tensions. The findings show that while both approaches approach the Nambu–Goto limit with 1/𝒯 corrections, NGKR overestimates the halving time by 20–35 % and predicts a different ultraviolet axion spectrum due to wavefront emission and loop rebound.

papers.title: On a model of quantum quadratic gravity in 7 + 1-dimensional spacetime
papers.abstract:
We consider a quadratic gravity model supplemented by the terms $
abla_{\mu}R
abla^{\mu}R$ and $(
abla^{2}R)^2$. For specific relations among the coupling constants, the action takes a perfect-square form. In the spatially flat FLRW model, we perform a reduction to a dynamical variable invariant under time reparameterizations. We construct a nonlinear change of variable that transforms the reduced action into the Gaussian action associated with the Wiener measure. An analysis of the transformation Jacobian within a time discretization singles out the case of $7+1$-dimensional spacetime, in which the Jacobian of the discrete transformation under consideration is independent of the dynamical variable. On this basis, we propose a formal representation of expectation values of observables in the reduced model as integrals with respect to the Wiener measure.
papers.summary: The authors construct a quadratic gravity model in 8 dimensions whose action can be written as a perfect square for special couplings, and they reduce the spatially flat FLRW dynamics to a single invariant variable that can be mapped to a Gaussian action via a nonlinear change of variables. This mapping allows them to express expectation values of observables as integrals over the Wiener measure, with the Jacobian simplifying only in the 7+1 dimensional case.

papers.title: Inverse design of scalar-tensor EFT from odd-parity effective potentials
papers.abstract: We develop an inverse-design approach to the effective field theory (EFT) of perturbations in scalar-tensor gravity around static and spherically symmetric backgrounds with a timelike scalar-field gradient, taking the odd-parity effective potential as input and reconstructing compatible background and EFT data. As analytically tractable examples, we construct explicit realizations of the P\"oschl-Teller potential, for which the quasinormal-mode spectrum can be obtained in closed form. We then study the Regge-Wheeler potential of general relativity and its parametrized deformations, showing how both can be realized within the scalar-tensor EFT. In particular, the latter realizations provide a route to interpreting phenomenological constraints on potential deformations from black hole ringdown observations in terms of the underlying EFT data.
papers.summary: This work develops an inverse‑design method for the odd‑parity sector of scalar‑tensor gravity, reconstructing background and EFT functions from a prescribed effective potential. The authors illustrate the technique with the exactly solvable Pöschl‑Teller potential and show how the Regge–Wheeler potential of GR and its deformations can be embedded in the EFT framework, providing a bridge between ringdown phenomenology and underlying scalar‑tensor dynamics.

papers.title: Systematic High Overtone Expansion of Kerr Quasinormal Modes
papers.abstract: We develop a systematic method to compute the high overtone expansion of Kerr quasinormal modes on normal angular branches to arbitrary order. We first obtain the expansion of the angular eigenvalue at large frequencies by a simple polynomial recursion. Using this result in an alternative form of the radial Teukolsky equation, we find that all the WKB corrections are defined on a fixed genus-one spectral curve, and that the quantum periods at the second and higher orders are expressed in terms of only two elliptic periods. This allows us to determine the expansion coefficients order by order. We confirm that the truncated expansions reproduce quasinormal frequencies obtained by solving the angular and radial equations directly, for scalar, electromagnetic and gravitational fields. We also compare the scalar results with the exact WKB analysis of extremal Kerr black holes.
papers.summary: This work presents a systematic high‑overtone expansion for Kerr quasinormal modes using a polynomial recursion for angular eigenvalues and a WKB analysis on a genus‑one spectral curve, yielding explicit expressions for quantum periods in terms of elliptic integrals. The authors verify the expansions against numerical solutions for scalar, electromagnetic, and gravitational perturbations, and compare scalar results with exact WKB for extremal Kerr.

papers.title: Gauge-parameter cancellation and finite form factors in one-loop quark scattering in the refined Gribov-Zwanziger framework
papers.abstract: We calculate the one-loop amplitude for distinct-flavor massless quark scattering in a local BRST-invariant refined Gribov-Zwanziger theory with minimally coupled quarks. The constraint determinant and two dynamical quark flavors are included in the action and in the loop sum. Retaining the refined Gribov-Zwanziger masses in the free field matrix, we combine the mixed self-energy insertion, complete vertex and box corrections, and external-leg residues. The difference between a general linear covariant gauge and a reference gauge vanishes symbolically after removal of the Stueckelberg regulator in the specified dimensional prescription. We separate ultraviolet and infrared poles, retaining contributions hidden by scaleless integrals and by the order of mass and dimensional limits. Local modified-minimal-subtraction counterterms close the ultraviolet poles, and the remaining infrared poles cancel in the stated nonzero-mass domain. The finite answer is supplied as eight color-spin form factors over a thirty-entry scalar integral inventory, with all 144 finite-function coefficients provided electronically. The result defines a partonic amplitude on a specified analytic branch; it does not assume colored asymptotic states or establish an inclusive next-to-leading-order cross section.
papers.summary: This paper presents a complete one-loop calculation of distinct-flavor massless quark scattering in a BRST-invariant refined Gribov–Zwanziger framework, demonstrating gauge-parameter cancellation and providing explicit finite form factors after careful treatment of UV/IR divergences. The authors supply a full set of color–spin form factors and scalar integrals, offering a detailed partonic amplitude that could serve as a benchmark for future higher-order or nonperturbative studies in gauge theory.

papers.title: Hot and dense QCD equation of state from the complex Langevin equation
papers.authors: Michael Mandl, D\'enes Sexty, Daniel Unterhuber
papers.abstract: We discuss the QCD equation of state at temperatures above the crossover and for high baryon chemical potentials, obtained via the first ever complex Langevin simulations at the physical pion mass. In particular, we present continuum-extrapolated results for the energy, entropy, and enthalpy densities, as well as for the specific heat capacity as a function of baryon chemical potential and temperature.
papers.summary: This paper presents continuum‑extrapolated results for the QCD equation of state at high temperatures and baryon chemical potentials using complex Langevin simulations at the physical pion mass. It reports energy, entropy, enthalpy densities and specific heat as functions of temperature and chemical potential, providing new data for the hot and dense QCD regime.

papers.title: Nonlinear response and retarded three-point correlators of charge transport
papers.abstract: We study nonlinear response of charge transport in relativistic kinetic theory within the relaxation time approximation. For a classical gas of massless charged particles coupled to an external $U(1)$ gauge field, we organize the Boltzmann equation perturbatively in the source and derive a recursive solution for the distribution function to arbitrary response order. At second order we analytically obtain fully retarded three-point correlators at generic frequencies and momenta, verify the Ward identities implied by charge conservation. We also discuss the general properties of these correlators, including their analytic structure, consistency limits, and relation to Schwinger--Keldysh effective theories of diffusive fluctuations.
papers.summary: This paper develops a recursive solution to the Boltzmann equation in the relaxation time approximation for a massless charged gas, enabling analytic computation of fully retarded three‑point correlators of charge transport at arbitrary frequencies and momenta. The authors verify Ward identities, analyze analytic structure, and connect the results to Schwinger–Keldysh effective theories of diffusive fluctuations.

papers.title: Two-loop BRST-restoring finite counter-terms for chiral non-abelian gauge theories
papers.abstract: We study the renormalization of anomaly-free chiral $SU(N)$ gauge theories without scalar fields through two-loop order. We adopt the Breitenlohner--Maison--'t Hooft--Veltman (BMHV) scheme for the treatment of $\gamma_5$ in dimensional regularization. This prescription induces spurious breaking of BRST symmetry, requiring finite symmetry-restoring counter-terms in addition to the subtraction of ultraviolet divergences. We derive these counter-terms for a general, possibly reducible fermion representation, thus restoring the BRST symmetry, through two loops.
papers.summary: This paper computes the finite counter‑terms required to restore BRST symmetry in anomaly‑free chiral SU(N) gauge theories up to two loops, using the BMHV scheme for γ5. The authors provide explicit expressions for arbitrary fermion representations, ensuring consistent renormalization without breaking gauge invariance.

papers.title: Probing micron-range fifth forces with cold atoms in optical tweezer arrays
papers.abstract: We propose a new method to search for fifth forces at micron scales, by resonantly exciting the motional state of ground-state-cooled atoms in optical tweezer arrays. We develop a homodyne readout protocol based on sideband thermometry, which can approach the Standard Quantum Limit, and expand the discovery reach for fifth forces by up to four orders of magnitude compared to existing constraints. We show that this level of sensitivity can also probe well-motivated models of extra dimensions beyond the current tabletop state of the art, by leveraging the parametric enhancement of higher-dimensional gravity.
papers.summary: This paper proposes using resonantly excited cold atoms in optical tweezer arrays to probe micron-scale fifth forces, achieving sensitivity up to four orders of magnitude beyond current limits. It also demonstrates that the method can test extra-dimensional gravity models via parametric enhancement.

papers.title: Quantum Observables of Nonperturbative Superradiant Scattering
papers.authors: Asimina Arvanitaki, Savas Dimopoulos, Marios Galanis, Derek J. Li
papers.abstract: Inelastic scattering from $N$ coherent spins, or any two-state system, scales as $N^2$, invalidating the Born approximation at large $N$ even at weak coupling. We develop a nonperturbative theory of this superradiant scattering and its backreaction on the spins. Since one particle can exchange many quanta, the target's energy-transfer and energy-variance rates keep their favorable $N^2$ scaling even after the cross section saturates, unless a conservation law limits each encounter to exchange of one quantum. We apply the theory to millicharged-particle searches, as well as neutron and charged-particle beams that can test quantum protocols for detecting cosmic relics.
papers.summary: This work develops a nonperturbative framework for superradiant scattering from a large ensemble of two‑level systems, showing that the $N^2$ scaling of energy transfer persists even after cross‑section saturation. The authors apply the formalism to searches for millicharged particles and to precision tests of quantum protocols using neutron and charged‑particle beams.

papers.title: Searching for Dark Photons and ALPs using Gamma-rays from Nuclear Reactors
papers.authors: Lucia Angel, Manfred Lindner, Farinaldo S. Queiroz, Bilge S. Solak
papers.abstract: Nuclear reactors are intense sources of MeV gamma rays, produced in fission, radiative neutron capture and the de-excitation of fission products. Building on earlier phenomenological studies, we present a detector-independent description of the production of light, weakly coupled particles by reactor gamma rays and of their detection through scattering, absorption and decay in a nearby detector. We consider kinetically mixed dark photons, produced and detected through Compton-like processes, and axion-like particles (ALPs) coupled to photons, electrons and nucleons, produced through Primakoff conversion, Compton-like scattering and magnetic nuclear transitions such as the $2.23~\mathrm{MeV}$ line of $p(n,\gamma)d$. As a concrete application, we derive the projected sensitivities of the CONUS+ germanium experiment at the Leibstadt reactor and of a conceivable $100$-kg CONUS100 upgrade. For sub-MeV dark photons, CONUS+ and CONUS100 reach kinetic mixings of $\epsilon\simeq1.65\times10^{-5}$ and $1.2\times10^{-5}$, respectively, for $0.5~\mathrm{keV}\lesssim m_{A'}\lesssim0.5~\mathrm{MeV}$. For ALPs, we show that CONUS100 can probe an unexplored region of parameter space at MeV masses, in particular through $a\to e^+e^-$ decays of ALPs emitted in the deuteron line, assuming a energy window extended to $10~\mathrm{MeV}$.
papers.summary: This paper develops a detector-independent framework for producing and detecting light weakly coupled particles from reactor gamma rays, focusing on kinetically mixed dark photons and axion-like particles. It projects sensitivities for the CONUS+ and a 100‑kg upgrade, achieving kinetic mixing reach of ~10^-5 for sub‑MeV dark photons and probing unexplored MeV‑mass ALP parameter space via deuteron line decays.

papers.title: Odds Estimation for Supermassive Black Hole Binaries in Local Core Galaxies
papers.abstract: Supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs) are expected products of massive galaxy mergers, but identifying binaries in nearby galaxies remains challenging. We combine simulated massive-galaxy assembly histories from IllustrisTNG with a semi-analytic core-scouring model to connect observable core galaxy properties to the probability of hosting a bound SMBHB at z=0. We (i) construct a core galaxy population using an observationally motivated galaxy stellar mass function, (ii) model binary evolution through dynamical friction, stellar hardening, and gravitational-wave emission, and (iii) perform logistic regressions with five observable predictors: stellar mass deficit, stellar mass, central density, central velocity dispersion, and effective radius. The resulting models perform well on simulated systems, achieving a pseudo-$R^2$ of $0.51\pm0.03$, accuracy $0.95\pm0.01$, precision $0.92\pm0.03$, and recall $0.82\pm0.04$. Uncoalesced binaries are typically compact, with separations peaking near 0.3 pc, though only $\sim0.3\%$ emit in the pulsar timing array band. Applying the model to observed core galaxies, we identify eight nearby galaxies more likely than not to host SMBHBs. Of those eight host candidates, we note Messier 86 (NGC 4406) as a particularly likely example that was similarly identified using independent means and therefore warrants future follow-up.
papers.summary: This study uses IllustrisTNG simulations and a core-scouring model to predict the probability that local core galaxies host supermassive black hole binaries, achieving high classification performance with logistic regression on observable galaxy parameters. The authors identify eight nearby galaxies, including M86, as promising SMBHB candidates, noting that only a tiny fraction of binaries emit in the pulsar timing array band.

papers.title: Fate of Quantum Magic
papers.authors: Liuke Lyu, Erik S. S{\o}rensen, William Witczak-Krempa
papers.abstract: Magic, a quantum resource distinct from entanglement, measures departure from states stabilized by products of Pauli operators. Such stabilizer states can be maximally entangled yet admit efficient classical description: quantum advantage requires magic. We develop a powerful framework to evaluate the degree of magic in generic many-body states. We use it to study the fate of magic under thermal and dynamical evolution. In the transverse field Ising model, we find a thermal sudden death of magic that saturates with system size, and occurs after the death of entanglement. We reach similar conclusions in generic spin chains, and in the Kitaev quantum spin liquid on the honeycomb lattice, where the threshold shows an intricate dependence on subregion shape. We then study how magic equilibrates after a quantum quench. In quenches of generic spin chains, the magic of a subregion typically dies before entanglement, contrary to thermal trajectories. An explanation is given in terms of the geometry of non-magical states. As a third type of trajectory, we examine the fate of magic with separation with an appropriate notion of non-local magic and establish a sudden death. Finally, we show how to experimentally witness a volume law of frame-robust magic in quantum materials by using neutron scattering.
papers.summary: This work introduces a framework for quantifying quantum magic, a resource beyond entanglement, and applies it to spin models and the Kitaev honeycomb liquid, revealing sudden death of magic in thermal and quench dynamics. The authors also propose experimental detection via neutron scattering, but the study does not directly address the physicist's interests in holography, celestial amplitudes, or related mathematical structures.

papers.title: Nucleon Wave Functions from QCD Vacuum Topology
papers.abstract: Instantons, as topologically nontrivial gauge field configurations, provide a microscopic mechanism for chiral symmetry breaking and the $U_A(1)$ anomaly in QCD. Within the instanton liquid model (ILM), instantons generate multi-fermion interactions governed by their density and size. Using this framework, we develop a microscopic description of the nucleon based on instanton-induced quark--quark correlations. We derive the diquark interaction kernels arising from single instantons and instanton--anti-instanton molecules, revealing a strong attraction in the scalar channel and weaker correlations in the spin-one channels. Embedding these interactions in a covariant, permutation-symmetric Bethe--Salpeter--Faddeev equation yields a nucleon mass $m_N=939.53~{\rm MeV}$, with a predominantly scalar-diquark component ($98\%$) and a small axial-vector admixture ($2\%$) around the mass pole. Despite its small weight, the small admixture generates substantial spin--isospin interference, yielding an axial charge $g_A=1.265$, close to experiment. The resulting covariant amplitude is analytically continued to the light front to obtain the leading three-quark wave function. The corresponding unpolarized, helicity, and transversity parton distributions, along with their QCD-evolved moments, provide a direct connection to lattice QCD calculations and global-fit analyses. Our results show that the topology of the QCD vacuum organizes not only the nucleon mass and spin structure, but also its leading valence partonic content, providing a microscopic foundation for a more complete description including confinement and higher Fock components.
papers.summary: Using the instanton liquid model, the authors derive scalar-diquark dominated nucleon wave functions via a covariant Bethe–Salpeter–Faddeev equation, reproducing the physical nucleon mass and axial charge. The resulting light-front wave function yields valence parton distributions that can be compared directly with lattice QCD and global fits.

papers.title: Ten-loop fixed-dimension renormalization-group functions of the three-dimensional O(N) model from distributed GPU-accelerated parametric integration
papers.abstract:
The renormalization-group functions $ eta$, $\eta$ and $
u$ of the three-dimensional $O(N)$ model in fixed dimension (massive zero-momentum scheme) were known to eighth order in the coupling. We extend them to tenth order, and $ eta$ to eleventh, for general $N$, which requires the two- and four-point functions to ten loops (1,593,254 graphs at the last order), and re-evaluate all lower orders. Through the Callan-Symanzik equation every coefficient follows from per-order sums that are linear in finite, zero-momentum $ ar R$-subtracted parametric integrals, one per graph, which we sample on GPUs by tropical Monte Carlo with densities adapted to the forest terms. The computation reproduces the known sums from two to seven loops within three standard deviations and agrees at ninth and tenth order, at lower precision, with an independent route through an intermediate scheme. The new coefficients have relative uncertainties of a few $10^{-5}$ or better, and the eighth-order coefficients of $\eta$ and $
u$ improve by factors of 120 and 4. The time needed to integrate an order to fixed relative precision grows by only 2.4-2.9 per loop from seven loops on, while the construction of the integrands still grows factorially and, at tenth order, costs more than the integration. Resummed, the tenth-order series give $
u=0.62997(51)$, $\eta=0.0333(18)$ and $\omega=0.803(14)$ for $N=1$, against $0.62997097(12)$, $0.036297612(48)$ and $0.82968(23)$ from the conformal bootstrap; at $N=3$ the deviations grow, so that the uncertainty is now dominated by the resummation rather than by the coefficients. Every result is generated automatically from, or checked against, a public ledger of independent, exactly pooled runs, hosted on GitHub, to which anyone is welcome to contribute computing time.
papers.summary: This work extends the fixed-dimension renormalization‑group functions of the 3D O(N) model to tenth order, using GPU‑accelerated parametric integration of over 1.5 million graphs, achieving unprecedented precision for β, η, and ν. The resulting high‑order series, when resummed, yield critical exponents that are competitive with conformal bootstrap results, offering a powerful benchmark for perturbative RG studies.

papers.title: Emergence of an acoustic black hole in a lattice model
papers.abstract: We build an acoustic black hole in a lattice model: a draining vortex evolved by the local collide-and-stream rule of a lattice-Boltzmann model, with no acoustic metric imposed, the geometry being measured from the steady state. A horizon emerges, first located from the measured Mach profile and then confirmed by phonon ray tracing on the measured metric, and the ringdown after a perturbation follows approximately the quasinormal frequencies of the draining bathtub. The residual departures are traced to the cell-scale structure of the horizon, which is not an ideal absorber. We model it in two ways: as a reflective horizon on the ideal bathtub, with two free parameters (the modulus and phase of the reflectivity), and as the sonic point of the realised flow absorbing in its own frame, with no adjustable parameter. The second describes the horizon and the non-rotating spectrum best. Superradiance has two ingredients: the emergent geometry, which amplifies in a loss-free calculation on the measured metric, and the horizon, whose absorption frame sets the width and strength of the amplified band but leaves no trace in the ringdown. Both models are used to examine superradiance, which has not been observed in the present toy model: whether the lattice hole superradiates dynamically remains open. The lattice leaves its own imprint as well: a fourfold anisotropy of the sonic surface and a surface gravity set by the cell-scale structure of the horizon.
papers.summary: This paper constructs an acoustic black hole in a lattice-Boltzmann simulation, demonstrating horizon formation and quasinormal ringing without imposing an acoustic metric. It studies superradiance and horizon reflectivity, highlighting lattice‑scale effects on the emergent geometry.

papers.title: Balancing tautological intersection numbers
papers.abstract: We prove the three balancing inequalities conjectured by the authors about 20 years ago: moving one unit from a larger index to a smaller one cannot decrease a mixed tautological intersection number, whether the two distinguished insertions are psi classes, kappa classes, or Hodge Chern classes.
papers.summary: The paper establishes three previously conjectured balancing inequalities for mixed tautological intersection numbers on moduli spaces of curves, showing that redistributing weight from a larger index to a smaller one never decreases the value. This result clarifies the combinatorial structure of psi, kappa, and Hodge class intersections, but does not directly address the physicist's interests in holography or related areas.

papers.title: Covariant phase space analysis of static spherical vacua in power-law $f(R)$ gravity
papers.authors: Mariam Campbell, Eduardo Bittencourt, Peter K. S. Dunsby
papers.abstract: We formulate the static, spherically symmetric vacuum equations of power-law metric $f(R)$ gravity as a covariant autonomous system using the $(1+1+2)$ formalism. The finite critical sets include the scale-invariant Clifton--Barrow solution, a Minkowski endpoint shared by the Schwarzschild family, and degenerate boundaries of the normalized chart. The Clifton--Barrow equilibrium is an outward-radial attractor over a positive interval of the power-law parameter, whereas the Schwarzschild endpoint is a saddle of the polynomially extended system. Poincar\'e compactification, supplemented by secondary and weighted charts, resolves several asymptotic regimes. In particular, normally attracting sheets at large normalized curvature occur in the positive-curvature sector and are separated from the negative-curvature Clifton--Barrow equilibrium. Metric reconstruction also identifies a selected scalar-flat family with a regular throat, one asymptotically flat end, and a curvature-singular end. These results organize the regular reduced chart and the boundary regimes resolved here; they do not constitute a complete classification of static spherical vacua. All stability statements concern the static radial flow.
papers.summary: This work recasts the static, spherically symmetric vacuum equations of power‑law f(R) gravity into a covariant autonomous system using the (1+1+2) formalism, identifying critical points such as the Clifton–Barrow solution and a Minkowski endpoint. The authors analyze the stability of these equilibria via Poincaré compactification, revealing attractor behavior for the Clifton–Barrow solution and saddle behavior for the Schwarzschild endpoint, and construct a scalar‑flat solution with a regular throat.

papers.title: HWF Analysis of TRN Black Holes
papers.authors: Ashfaque Ahmad, Sudhir Kumar Gupta, Abbas Ali
papers.abstract: We extend the horizon wave-function (HWF) formalism to a spherically symmetric, charged, spinless quantum source in $\mathcal{D} + 1$ dimensional spacetime geometry and construct the HWFs associated with inner- as well as outer-horizons of the Tangherlini--Reissner--Nordstr\"om (TRN) black hole. The corresponding black hole formation probabilities, $P_{\rm BH}^{\pm}$, are also calculated and their sensitivities due to various source parameters including charge, mass, and $\mathcal{D}$ are analysed as well. Our analysis reveals that the ratio of inner- to outer-horizon probabilities, $P_{\rm BH}^{-}/P_{\rm BH}^{+}$, changes drastically from being unity as the source departs away from being in the extremal limit defined by $\alpha$ ($\to 1$ for extremal case). Furthermore, black hole formation probabilities are found to be highly suppressed for higher values of $\mathcal{D}$, particularly for the source mass, $m \lesssim \Lambda_{\mathcal{D}}$, e.g., for $\alpha = 0.5$, the ratio, $P_{\rm BH}^{+}(\mathcal{D} = 5)/P_{\rm BH}^{+}(\mathcal{D}=10)$ turn out to be approximately associated with $\mathcal{D}$ spatial-dimensions.
papers.summary: This paper extends the horizon wave-function formalism to charged, spherically symmetric quantum sources in D+1 dimensions, deriving the wave functions for both inner and outer horizons of Tangherlini–Reissner–Nordström black holes. It computes the corresponding black hole formation probabilities and studies their dependence on charge, mass, and dimensionality, finding strong suppression in higher dimensions and a dramatic change in the inner-to-outer horizon probability ratio away from extremality.

papers.title: Enhanced Signal and Excited-State Control in Nonlocal Lattice Correlators
papers.authors: Shi-Yi Zhong, Jian-Hui Zhang, Dian-Jun Zhao
papers.abstract: Nonlocal correlation functions underpin lattice calculations of parton physics. However, their extraction is limited by a rapidly deteriorating signal-to-noise ratio with increasing Euclidean separation and hadron momentum, and by excited-state contamination. We propose a new fitting strategy that enhances control over both: by taking the ratio of nonlocal to local correlators, we can project out the dominant ground-state dynamics with a signal that is much cleaner and far less sensitive to excited states than the conventional approach. We demonstrate the method on the quark and gluon PDF, the quark GPD and TMDPDF. The results are consistent with those from the conventional three-point/two-point ratio fit but exhibit markedly improved precision and stability, and extend the accessible range to larger hadron momenta. For nonforward matrix elements such as GPDs, our strategy greatly simplifies the analysis procedure. Our method applies to general Dirac and momentum structures, for connected and disconnected contributions, and extends naturally to other nonlocal correlators, making it immediately deployable in existing lattice programs toward precision hadron structure.
papers.summary: The authors introduce a ratio-based fitting strategy that suppresses excited-state contamination and improves signal-to-noise in nonlocal lattice correlators, enabling more precise extraction of parton distributions at higher hadron momenta. The technique is broadly applicable to quark/gluon PDFs, GPDs, TMDs, and other nonlocal observables, simplifying analysis for both connected and disconnected contributions.

papers.title: Thermodynamic Crossovers in Supercritical Matter: One, No One, and One Hundred Thousand
papers.abstract: Beyond a critical point, two thermodynamic phases become continuously connected, without being separated by any thermodynamic singularity. The paradigmatic example is the liquid-gas transition, where several criteria have been proposed to distinguish liquid-like and gas-like regimes within the supercritical region. Recently, a pair of thermodynamic crossover lines, $L^\pm$, was introduced to address a proposed incompatibility of previous definitions with the universal critical behavior of the Ising model. These lines divide the supercritical region into three regimes, meet only at the critical point, and obey the expected critical scaling laws. Here, we demonstrate that these requirements do not uniquely determine the crossover boundaries. Instead, infinitely many pairs of lines satisfy the same conditions, with different choices of thermodynamic paths selecting different crossover boundaries. We further show that the Lee-Yang formalism, despite providing an intrinsic characterization of critical singularities, does not resolve this ambiguity in defining real-axis crossover boundaries. Restricting to regular probing paths that respect the $Z_2$ symmetry of the critical point recovers the Widom and $L^\pm$ prescriptions asymptotically. This restriction, however, is a choice of protocol rather than a property of the system, and even then two inequivalent prescriptions survive. Our results demonstrate that universal critical behavior alone does not select privileged supercritical thermodynamic crossover boundaries. While such lines may identify physically meaningful changes in thermodynamic, structural, or transport properties, their precise locations and the widths of the regions they delimit remain dependent on the operational criteria used to define them.
papers.summary: The paper examines how universal critical scaling of the Ising model allows for infinitely many thermodynamic crossover lines in the supercritical regime, showing that the choice of path determines the boundaries. It demonstrates that even Lee‑Yang zeros cannot uniquely fix these crossover lines, implying that operational definitions rather than intrinsic physics set the supercritical phase boundaries.

papers.title: Phenomenological implications of cosmic (super)strings with time-varying tension
papers.authors: Anastasios Avgoustidis, Edmund J. Copeland, Adam Moss, Juhan Raidal, Filippo Revello, Gonzalo Villa
papers.abstract: Cosmic strings and cosmic superstrings could have formed in the early universe. In a particular class of models, the tension associated with these defects is time dependent, either because the strings themselves are composed of evolving moduli fields, or because they are directly coupled to evolving scalar fields leading to an effective time dependence in the string tension. Here we take seriously the possibility of this time dependence and investigate the phenomenological consequences of such an evolution, comparing the results to the more traditional case of a fixed time independent tension. In particular, for five different time varying models, motivated by different possible forms of evolution of the string tension, we evaluate their Gravitational Wave (GW) contributions as well as their impact on the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB). Performing an MCMC analysis of the models we find there are indeed interesting spectral signatures in the GW emission at frequencies between the current PTA and interferometer data, but the signatures are not unique to these strings, making them hard to pin down using current data. However, we do find cosmic strings with evolving tension fit the GW data as well as other favoured models.
papers.summary: The authors study cosmic (super)strings whose tension evolves over time, computing their gravitational wave spectra and CMB signatures across five models. They find that while the time‑varying tension can produce distinctive GW features between PTA and interferometer bands, these signatures are not unique and the models fit current data comparably to standard fixed‑tension strings.

papers.title: Rotation overcharges vectorized black holes
papers.authors: Shengjun Guo, Guangzai Ye, Peng Liu
papers.abstract: A charged black hole has a ceiling: extremality bounds the charge that a given mass and spin can support. Vector hair has so far only lowered it. In the Einstein--Maxwell--Vector (EMV) model, where a massless vector field couples nonminimally to the electromagnetic invariant, the spherically symmetric vectorized Reissner--Nordstr\"om black holes are strictly undercharged: vector hair is paid for in charge. Whether this ceiling is a property of the vector field or merely of spherical symmetry has remained open, because spherical symmetry hides the hair's mass as well: its Komar mass vanishes identically and the exact identity $M_V=2\Omega_HJ_V$ degenerates to $0=0$. Rotation lifts both degeneracies at once. We construct the rotating solutions of the model, the first in this setting, and find that the hair's mass is not a free parameter but a second-order invariant of the rotational response, fixed by $M_V=2\Omega_HJ_V$. Above a coupling threshold the ceiling gives way: the domain of existence crosses the extremal Kerr--Newman bound, reaching $q=Q/M>1$ with $q^2+\chi^2$ up to $1.84$, while at $\alpha=5$ the maximum charge stays below it. The shadow is where the hair becomes visible. At $(q,\chi)=(0.9947,0.10)$, near the extremal bound, the hair contributes an ellipticity of $8.30\%$, against $0.44\%$ from the charge and $0.06\%$ from rotation --- a factor of $19$ that charging a Kerr black hole cannot mimic; at the overcharged solution $(q,\chi)=(1.2527,0.10)$ the total ellipticity reaches $25.6\%$. Whether the branch is ghost-free remains open, but the existing no-go criteria do not settle it: they assume a background and a dispersion relation that do not hold here.
papers.summary: This paper constructs the first rotating solutions in the Einstein–Maxwell–Vector model, showing that vector hair lifts the degeneracy of extremality bounds and can push the charge-to-mass ratio beyond the Kerr–Newman limit. The authors find that the hair contributes significantly to the shadow ellipticity, offering a potential observable signature of overcharged black holes.

papers.title: Heavy-Particle Effective Theory: from On-Shell Formalism to Gravitational Compton Amplitudes
papers.authors: Yong-Kang Li, Yi-Ning Wang, Jiang-Hao Yu
papers.abstract: We formulate on-shell heavy-particle effective theory (HPET) amplitudes by projecting the spinor-helicity variables onto the $SU(2)$ little group of a timelike reference velocity $v^{\mu}$. Retaining both large and small components of the velocity-projected spinors gives an intermediate velocity-projected amplitudes in which reparameterization invariance can be imposed before expanding in the inverse heavy-particle mass. Integrating out the small component then yields HPET amplitudes organized by heavy-particle power counting, with a direct correspondence to local operators at fixed order. We determine the three-point velocity-projected amplitudes for two equal-mass particles of arbitrary spin $S$ coupled to a soft massless boson of helicity $h$. Four-point gravitational Compton amplitudes can be constructively obtained using velocity-projected three-point amplitudes, and expanded into HPET amplitudes which is free of spurious poles up to sub-leading order. As a gravitational application, we show that the projected gravitational minimal coupling reproduces the Kerr spin-induced multipoles up to order $2S$, and find the classical limits of the tree-level elastic gravitational scattering and gravitational Compton amplitudes agreed with the literature up to contact terms undetermined by factorization.
papers.summary: The paper develops a heavy-particle effective theory (HPET) using on-shell spinor-helicity variables projected onto a timelike reference velocity, enabling systematic construction of velocity-projected amplitudes and their expansion in inverse mass. It applies this framework to compute gravitational Compton amplitudes, reproducing Kerr multipoles and matching known classical scattering results up to contact terms.

papers.title: Quasinormal-mode encounters: Pseudospectra near Kerr--Newman exceptional points
papers.abstract: Exceptional points (EPs), at which two quasinormal frequencies and their eigenvectors coalesce, can strongly enhance the spectral instability of black hole quasinormal modes. We investigate this behavior in Kerr--Newman spacetimes through pseudospectra and condition numbers for neutral massless scalar fields and coupled gravitoelectromagnetic (GE) perturbations. For the scalar field, we follow the $(\ell,m)=(1,1)$ spheroidal branch and derive the energy norm from the stress-energy tensor. For GE perturbations, we use a coupled four-field system equipped with a positive radiative energy. At the selected near-EP backgrounds, the condition numbers of both modes in the close pair exceed those of the two more-damped modes shown for comparison at the same background. Along a matched GE parameter path, the frequency splitting follows a square-root law and the condition numbers grow as the inverse square root of the distance to the EP. The pseudospectral contours resolve the transition from individual-mode sensitivity to the collective response of the pair. Within the discretized problems and energy norms considered here, these results quantify the amplification of spectral instability near EPs and provide a basis for studying their contribution to black-hole ringdown.
papers.summary: The paper studies how exceptional points in the spectrum of quasinormal modes of Kerr–Newman black holes amplify spectral instability, using pseudospectra and condition numbers for scalar and gravitoelectromagnetic perturbations. It shows that near an EP the mode pair obeys a square‑root frequency splitting and that the condition numbers diverge as the inverse square root of the distance to the EP, offering a quantitative handle on mode sensitivity during black‑hole ringdown.

papers.title: A Lighter QCD-Axion from Small Instantons
papers.authors: Sourav Bera, Susobhan Chattopadhyay, Rick S. Gupta
papers.abstract: We propose models where the QCD axion mass can be much smaller than the standard expectation. We show that this is possible in models where both QCD and the Standard Model flavor structure get modified in the ultraviolet (UV). In these models, both the axion mass and the up-quark Yukawa can receive sizeable non-perturbative contributions from instantons in the UV. If both these effects are carefully taken into account, the QCD axion is not necessarily heavier than usual expectations and can, in fact, be much lighter. We show that if small instanton contributions account for a large fraction of the up-quark Yukawa, the QCD axion can be lighter than standard expectations whereas it is heavier otherwise. We propose two different models where this condition is realised: (1) one where the QCD gauge group emerges as a subgroup from a product of $SU(3)$ groups in the UV; and (2) a composite Higgs model that also implements partial compositeness. In both these models the QCD axion can lie not only in the region to the right of the QCD axion band but also far to its left. This is especially relevant for a range of proposed haloscope and helioscope experiments that will probe a region mostly to the left of the QCD band.
papers.summary: The authors propose UV models where small instanton effects reduce the QCD axion mass below standard expectations, linking it to the up‑quark Yukawa. They present two constructions—an SU(3) product gauge group and a partial‑compositeness Higgs model—that allow the axion to lie outside the conventional QCD band, relevant for upcoming haloscope searches.

papers.title: Gravitational-Wave Echoes and Greybody Cutoff from Logarithmic Throats at a Marginal-Trapping Threshold
papers.abstract: When a static, spherically symmetric configuration is brought close to a marginal-trapping threshold, it develops a long throat. As the nondegenerate minimum of $F=1-2m/r$ approaches zero, $F\simeq\Delta+\beta(r-R_M)^2$, the proper length across the throat grows as $-\ln\Delta/\sqrt\beta$, even though the local curvature stays finite. We study how axial gravitational waves propagate in an effective model of this throat, in which the lapse is parametrized as $N\propto F^{s/2}$. For $s>0$ the throat acts as a cavity behind the angular-momentum barrier, and waves come back out as echoes spaced by $T_{\rm echo}\simeq2\Lambda+\delta\propto\Delta^{-s/2}$, where $\Lambda$ is the optical length of the throat and $\delta$ does not depend on $\Delta$. We study four-dimensional, matter-supported quasi-black holes in which a regular centre caps the near-AdS$_2$ throat. These configurations provide a simplified model for investigating capped throats in horizonless microstate geometries. The echo delay in this model is controlled by the inverse redshift near the bottom of the throat, as in capped microstate geometries. This differs from thin-shell gravastars and wormholes, where the delay grows only logarithmically with the distance to the would-be horizon. Time-domain evolutions confirm the $\Delta^{-s/2}$ scaling over three decades in $\Delta$; for $s=0$ the throat becomes part of the barrier and no distinct echo appears. The barrier also imposes a greybody cutoff on the reflected spectrum, $1-\Gamma\simeq e^{-(\omega-f)/T}$, where $T$ is fixed by the curvature of the barrier and does not depend on the surface gravity of any horizon behind it. In this model, the prompt signal is the same whether the interior contains a horizon or a reflecting throat. In the horizonless case, however, the transmitted wave returns as echoes, restoring the high-frequency part of the full reflected spectrum.
papers.summary: The paper studies axial gravitational waves in a near‑marginal‑trapping throat, showing that the long throat acts as a cavity producing echoes with delay scaling as Δ^{-s/2}. It also finds a greybody cutoff independent of any horizon, illustrating how horizonless microstate geometries can mimic black hole signals.
